entries.title: Type scale: an app scale in the tokens, components on the role line heights (Tier 3)
entries.why: An app type scale. Page titles drop from 44 to 30px (`typography.h1`), section titles from 30 to 24px (`typography.h2`), card and dialog titles from 21 to 16px semibold (`typography.h3`), body keeps 16px on a 24px line. New: `typography.meta` (13/18, the secondary line under a name or title), with the primitives `font.size.150` (13px), `font.leading.18` and `font.leading.24`. Components set their text on the role line heights (20px for UI text, 18 for meta, 16 for captions) instead of 1.2, 1.35 and 1.5 ratios that landed off the 4px grid, descriptions and errors under fields read in meta (13px) instead of 12px with wide tracking, and a bold word inside a Banner title no longer jumps to black (900). In Bridge, the current nav entry keeps the medium weight of the others (color and plate say where you are), the "See it as" menu sets names in medium over a 13px muted line, and text that sets no line height inherits 1.5 of its size instead of 24px.

pr.title: Type scale: an app scale in the tokens, components on the role line heights (Tier 3)
pr.author: peterbono
pr.body:
Agent-authored (Claude Code). **Risk tier 3**: adds tokens (`font.size.150`, `font.leading.18`, `font.leading.24`, the `typography.meta` role) and changes the values of `typography.h1`, `h2`, `h3` and `body`. Needs the design and tech owners' approval. Do not merge without it.

## Summary

Type in Bridge felt wrong because the hierarchy jumped two or three steps at once (14 semibold ink over 12 regular grey), titles were sized for a poster (44px Fraunces page titles, 30px section titles, 21px card titles that wrapped to 3 lines in side cards), and 42% of rendered text sat on line heights off the 4px grid (16.8, 18.9, 21, 26 on 14px text) because components used 1.2 / 1.35 / 1.5 ratios. This PR sets one app type scale in the tokens and moves the shared components onto it, so every page follows without per-page patches.

## 1. Audit (prod, before)

Crawled with Playwright (deviceScaleFactor 2): Studio home, Explorations, an exploration, a build review, Library review, Studio Components, Quality, the "See it as" menu, Library home, Library Button page, plus 3 phone pages. Computed style of every visible text node, the two specimen pages (Typography, Tokens) left out.

| Metric | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Text nodes measured | 1260 | 1218 |
| Distinct size / line height / weight combos | 36 | 28 |
| Distinct line heights | 14 | 13 |
| Text on a line height off the 4px grid | 528 (42%) | 288 (24%, mostly buttons whose box sets the height) |
| Black (900) text | 13 | 0 |
| Sizes in use (F = Fraunces) | 12, 14, 16, 21, 21F, 30F, 44F, 64F | 12, 13, 14, 16, 21F (wordmark), 24F, 30F, 64F (Library hero) |

Top combinations before, and what was wrong:

| Count | Family size / line height weight | Examples | Issue |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 234 | Inst 14/20 400 | banner text, emails | on scale |
| 163 | Inst 14/18.9 400 | Breadcrumb, tables, side lists | off grid: `line-height-snug` 1.35 |
| 110 | Inst 14/20 500 | nav entries | on scale |
| 100 | Inst 14/16.8 500 | buttons | ratio 1.2 (inside a fixed-height control, harmless) |
| 92 | Inst 14/20 600 | current nav entry, names | weight jump: current entry grows wider than the others |
| 71 | Inst 14/18.9 600 | menu names, popover titles | 600 over a 12/400 grey line: two steps at once |
| 60 | Inst 14/26 400 | text that sets a size but no line height | inherits the body's 26px: 1.86 ratio |
| 52 | Inst 16/26 600 | home queue titles | body leading on a title |
| 50 | Inst 12/14.4 500 | product chips | 1.2 on 12px |
| 21 | Inst 12/16.2 500 | section labels (Products, Design system) | off grid |
| 16 | Fraunces 21/28 600 | wordmark | aliased to `h3`, so it would move with card titles |
| 15 | Inst 21/28 600 | card and section titles | oversized for an app card |
| 14 | Fraunces 30/38 600 | Recent explorations, Products | section title nearly as big as a page title |
| 13 | Inst 14/20 **900** | "Acme Design." in the banner | `<b>` inside a semibold title: `bolder` jumps to black |
| 6 | Inst 12/16.2 400 | "Design lead" under a name in See it as | 12px secondary under 14/600 |
| 5 | Fraunces 44/50 500 | "Good evening, Dana.", exploration title, "Button" | poster size on app screens; 3-line titles in side cards |

## 2. Benchmark

Measured in Chrome with canvas `measureText` on the real font files (x-height and cap height as a fraction of the em, width of a-z):

| Font | x-height | Cap height | a-z width |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Instrument Sans | 0.510 | 0.720 | 13.59 em |
| Inter | 0.546 | 0.728 | 13.92 em |
| SF Pro (system-ui) | 0.508 | 0.705 | 12.25 em |
| Fraunces | 0.470 | 0.700 | 13.96 em |

So Instrument Sans does **not** have a tall x-height: it matches SF Pro and is 7% shorter than Inter. What makes it read big is its width: about 11% wider than SF Pro. Equivalent sizes by x-height:

| Instrument Sans | Inter | SF Pro |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 12 | 11.2 | 12 |
| 13 | 12.1 | 13 |
| 14 | 13.1 | 14 |
| 16 | 14.9 | 16 |

Reference app densities (public UIs, Inter or system fonts):

| Element | Linear | Figma (UI3) | Notion | GitHub (Primer) | Bridge after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Nav item | 13 / 500 | 11-13 | 14 / 500 | 14 / 400 | 14 / 500 (= Inter 13) |
| Menu item | 13 / 400 | 11-12 | 14 | 14 | 14 / 400-500 |
| List row title | 13-14 / 500 | 11-13 | 14 / 500 | 14 / 600 | 14 / 500 (ui) or 16 / 600 (h3) |
| Secondary line | 12-13 / 400 muted | 11 | 12-13 muted | 12 muted | 13 / 400 muted (meta) |
| Section label | 12 / 500 | 11 / 600 | 12 / 500 | 12 / 600 | 12 / 500 wide (caption) |
| Card / dialog title | 14-15 / 500 | 13 / 600 | 16 / 600 | 14-16 / 600 | 16 / 600 (h3) |
| Page title | 15-20 / 500 | n/a | 32-40 / 700 (docs) | 24-32 / 400-600 | 30 Fraunces 500 (h1) |

Takeaway: 14px Instrument Sans is exactly Linear's 13px Inter and GitHub/Notion's 14px, so the UI size stays. The faults were the jumps, the oversized titles and the off-grid leading, not the base size.

## 3. The scale

| Role | Token | Size / line | Weight | Tracking | Color | Family | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Display | `typography.display` | 64 / 68 | 500 | -0.025em | default | Fraunces | Marketing and Library home hero only (unchanged) |
| Page title | `typography.h1` | **30 / 38** (was 44 / 50) | 500 | -0.015em | default | Fraunces | One per page |
| Section title | `typography.h2` | **24 / 32** (was 30 / 38) | **500** (was 600) | -0.01em | default | Fraunces | Sections inside a page |
| Card, dialog, panel title | `typography.h3` | **16 / 24** (was 21 / 28) | 600 | **0** | default | Instrument Sans | Card, dialog, drawer, group titles |
| Body | `typography.body` | 16 / **24** (was 26) | 400 | 0 | default | Instrument Sans | Leads, reading text, empty state sentences |
| UI | `typography.ui` | 14 / 20 | 400, 500 for names, nav, labels | 0 | default | Instrument Sans | Controls, nav, menu items, rows, cells |
| Meta (**new**) | `typography.meta` | **13 / 18** | 400 | 0 | muted | Instrument Sans | The line under a name or title: job, date, path, field description |
| Caption | `typography.caption` | 12 / 16 | 400, 500 + wide for section labels | 0 / +0.01em | muted | Instrument Sans | Badges, section labels, footnotes |
| Numbers | primitives | 21 / 28, 30 / 38 | 500 | tabular | default | Fraunces | Wordmark, KPI numbers |

Operate (Studio) vs read (Library): app screens run on `ui`, `meta`, `caption`, with `h3` for cards and `h1` once; `body` is for leads and sentences. Docs pages read in `body` and keep `display` for the hero. The tokens are shared, the difference is which roles a surface reaches for.

Rules (also written into docs/DESIGN-LANGUAGE.md):
- Never below 12px. `color.text.muted` already passes 4.5:1 on bg default, subtle, zone, surface default, raised and hover (contrast gate, 304 checks, 0 failing).
- One step at a time: a name over its secondary line changes size by one step (14 over 13), weight by one (500 over 400) and color. Never 600 over 400 at 12.
- The current nav entry is set apart by color and plate, not by weight, so it does not grow wider.
- Fraunces only for `display`, `h1`, `h2`, the wordmark and big numbers, never at 16px or below. A side card or panel under 400px wide takes `h3`, not `h2`, so its title stays on two lines.

Why 30 for page titles: Fraunces' x-height is 0.47, so 30px Fraunces reads like a 27px sans, the top of the GitHub range and well under Notion's doc titles. The h1 / h2 / h3 ratio is now 1.25 / 1.5, a clear ladder without the 44 to 21 cliff.

## 4. Implementation

Tokens (`packages/tokens`):
- `primitives/typography.tokens.json`: **adds** `font.size.150` (13px), `font.leading.18`, `font.leading.24`. No value of an existing primitive changes.
- `brands/bridge.tokens.json` and `brands/ocean.tokens.json`: `h1`, `h2`, `h3`, `body` re-pointed as in the table; **adds** `typography.meta` in both brands (ocean keeps its semibold headings and Plex Sans). `packages/core/src/brand.ts` lists `meta` among the text roles so new brands set its family.

Shared components (`packages/react`, typography properties only, plus one icon box that equals the title's line):
- UI text moves from `font-size-200` + 1.2 / 1.35 / 1.5 ratios to `typography-ui-size` / `typography-ui-line-height` (20px): Accordion, Breadcrumb, Card body, Checkbox, CheckboxGroup legend, Combobox items, Dialog, Drawer, EmptyState description, Field label, Form summary, Menu, Popover, RadioGroup, Select items, SidebarNav items, Switch, Table, Tabs panel, Toast (its icon box follows the 20px line).
- Secondary lines move from 12px with wide tracking to `typography.meta` (13/18): Field description and error, Checkbox, RadioGroup, Switch, Select and Combobox item descriptions, Accordion meta, PageHeader meta, CheckboxGroup and RadioGroup errors.
- Section labels get the caption line height (16px): Menu, Select and Combobox group labels, SidebarNav section title, Divider label, Table head.
- Banner: `b` / `strong` inside the title inherit its weight (no more 900).
- `component-specs.json` regenerated; the drafted Toast spec updated to the new text tokens and its `codeHash` refreshed.

Bridge (`apps/docs-site`, shell-level only, no page layout touched):
- `site.css`: root line height is the 1.5 ratio instead of the body's px value, so text that sets a size but no line height stops inheriting 26px; the wordmark (`.logo-word`, `.topbar-space`) is pinned to 21/28 so it does not move with `h3`; the current nav entry keeps the medium weight.
- `studio-app.css`: the same for the Studio rail's current entry.
- `demo-home.css`: "See it as" names in medium over a 13px meta line.
- Library Typography page role notes follow the new scale.

## 5. Before / after

Before: prod. After: prod with this branch's built `tokens.css`, changed CSS modules (selectors mapped to prod's hashed class names) and changed shell CSS injected, so both columns show the same data. Desktop 1440x900 and phone 390x844, deviceScaleFactor 2.

| Screen | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Studio home | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/the-bridge-company/ai-design-system-demo/2047ae57137f3009cc017106464b6044484bf3f5/type-scale/before-home-dana.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/the-bridge-company/ai-design-system-demo/2047ae57137f3009cc017106464b6044484bf3f5/type-scale/after-home-dana.png) |
| Sidebar | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/the-bridge-company/ai-design-system-demo/2047ae57137f3009cc017106464b6044484bf3f5/type-scale/before-sidebar.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/the-bridge-company/ai-design-system-demo/2047ae57137f3009cc017106464b6044484bf3f5/type-scale/after-sidebar.png) |
| "See it as" menu | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/the-bridge-company/ai-design-system-demo/2047ae57137f3009cc017106464b6044484bf3f5/type-scale/before-menu.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/the-bridge-company/ai-design-system-demo/2047ae57137f3009cc017106464b6044484bf3f5/type-scale/after-menu.png) |
| Review (Library review, one by one) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/the-bridge-company/ai-design-system-demo/2047ae57137f3009cc017106464b6044484bf3f5/type-scale/before-library-review.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/the-bridge-company/ai-design-system-demo/2047ae57137f3009cc017106464b6044484bf3f5/type-scale/after-library-review.png) |
| Exploration page | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/the-bridge-company/ai-design-system-demo/2047ae57137f3009cc017106464b6044484bf3f5/type-scale/before-exploration.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/the-bridge-company/ai-design-system-demo/2047ae57137f3009cc017106464b6044484bf3f5/type-scale/after-exploration.png) |
| Library component (Button) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/the-bridge-company/ai-design-system-demo/2047ae57137f3009cc017106464b6044484bf3f5/type-scale/before-library-component.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/the-bridge-company/ai-design-system-demo/2047ae57137f3009cc017106464b6044484bf3f5/type-scale/after-library-component.png) |
| Phone, home | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/the-bridge-company/ai-design-system-demo/2047ae57137f3009cc017106464b6044484bf3f5/type-scale/before-phone-home.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/the-bridge-company/ai-design-system-demo/2047ae57137f3009cc017106464b6044484bf3f5/type-scale/after-phone-home.png) |
| Phone, exploration | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/the-bridge-company/ai-design-system-demo/2047ae57137f3009cc017106464b6044484bf3f5/type-scale/before-phone-exploration.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/the-bridge-company/ai-design-system-demo/2047ae57137f3009cc017106464b6044484bf3f5/type-scale/after-phone-exploration.png) |

What I see on them, critically:
- Better: page titles sit at app scale ("Deal pipeline cards", "Library review", "Good evening, Dana." now 30px); section titles ("Recent explorations", "Products") no longer compete with the page title; the side turn card title went from 44 to 24px; the menu reads as one even list (14/500 names over 13/400 muted jobs); the banner's "Acme Design." is semibold, not black; the current nav entry no longer grows.
- Still not right, outside this PR's shared layer:
  - The screenshots predate #1095, which (now on main) sets the exploration turn card title to the 21px display step; after the rebase that title stays at 21/28 Fraunces, 1 to 2 lines.
  - Home queue rows set their titles and bylines in `t-body` (16px): by the scale they should be `ui` 14/500 over `meta`. That is a per-component choice in ListCard / studio-home.css, left to the agent working there.
  - The Library docs nav current entry is still semibold (`site-nav.css`), left for a follow-up to keep this PR to the shared layer.

## UI quality bar

- Hierarchy through type: at most four sizes per Studio screen on the first view (home: 30, 24, 16, 14 plus 12 badges and the 21px wordmark).
- Gestalt similarity: every name / secondary pair uses ui + meta; every section label uses caption medium.
- Fitts: no control size changed (control heights are density tokens, untouched).
- Bridge brand: Fraunces keeps display, page and section titles; Instrument Sans everything else; one strong color.

## Conflicts to watch

- Rebased on main. Seven rules set Fraunces at the `h3` size (`.dc-body h2`, `.xp-plate-screen`, `.xp-turn-q` from #1095, `.li-plate`, `.lr-side-fam`, `.lr-chapter-name`, `.sg-title`): with `h3` at 16px they would have rendered Fraunces at 16, so they now name the 21/28 primitives they had before (`font-size-400`, `font-leading-28`). Any open PR adding Fraunces at `typography-h3-size` should do the same.
- The agent owning packages/react Stepper and count badges: this PR does not touch Stepper, Badge, `SidebarNav .count` or `Tabs .count`. It does change `SidebarNav.module.css` (section title and item line heights) and `Menu.module.css` (popup and group label line heights): typography lines only.
- Agents on docs-site alignment: the root line-height change in `site.css` lowers text that sets no line height from 24-26px lines to 1.5 (21px at 14px). Vertical rhythm of such blocks shrinks by a few px; spacing tokens are untouched.

## Checks

- `npm run tokens:build`: 304 contrast checks, 0 failing.
- `npm run lint:css`: clean.
- Typecheck: `@bridge-ds/react`, `@bridge-ds/core` clean. `apps/docs-site` reports only `node:*` type errors in `api/` and `dev/` from this worktree's linked node_modules, none in files touched here; CI is the reference.
- Vitest: packages/core, packages/tokens, packages/react, packages/toolbar, the Library views: all pass (the component-specs test now expects the role line heights; specs regenerated).
- Figma plugin tests (319): pass after updating two expectations that pinned the old values (Card header 21/28 to 16/24, Card body slot bound to `typography/ui/size`).
- CLI: the Bridge snapshot budget stays at 1,300,000 bytes; after #1107 it measures 1,108,240 with this branch (about 190 KB headroom).
- `npm run audit:docs`: passes (no regression, score over 95).
- Rebased on main after #1104 to #1110: conflicts in `SidebarNav.module.css` (main had already moved the item to the UI line height, kept main's comment) and `library-review.css` (took main's, re-applied the 21/28 pin to its two Fraunces labels); `component-specs.json` regenerated.
- `npm run build-storybook`: not run locally (8 GB machine), CI runs it.
- Changeset: tokens minor, react minor, core patch, docs-site patch.

pr.title: Revert the ship-from-Figma test (#468): color.bg.zone back to palette.primary.200
pr.author: peterbono
pr.body:
## What changed and why

Agent-authored (Claude Code). Reverts #468, the live test of **ship from Figma** agreed with Florian (merge, then revert): `color.bg.zone` Light goes back from `palette.primary.100` to `palette.primary.200`, and the test changeset leaves.

What the test showed: the Figma plugin opened #468 ready with `source: figma`; `/api/ship` armed it (auto-merge by the Bridge app, squash, approval "Bridge: shipped from Figma"); GitHub merged it at 12:04 once the required checks passed, with no person in the loop.

One bug found (core, reported to the owning session): the plugin then said "Held for a developer" because `libraryArrival` counts the non-required Vercel rate-limit failures as a failed check, and held is final, so it stopped polling before the merge.

## Risk tier

- [x] Tier 1, low: docs, stories, lint or a11y fixes, no visual or API change

## Authored by

- [x] AI agent (Claude), reviewed by a human before merge

## Design review checklist

- [x] Changeset added (the revert removes the test's changeset; nothing ships)
- [x] No lint rule disabled, no test or story deleted

pr.body:
## What changed and why Changes color.bg.zone in Light. Opened from the Bridge Figma plugin. Figma is the editing surface; this PR is the change. Pushed from Figma, so design-approved. Bridge merges it once the automatic checks pass; Undo is in History in Bridge Studio. ## Risk tier - [x] Tier 3: token change. From Figma: design-approved, ships once the checks pass ## Changes | Token | Tier | Change | Value (old -> new) | Contrast (before -> after) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `color.bg.zone` | Semantic | changed | Light: `palette.primary.200 (#cfe8ff)` -> `palette.primary.100 (#e4f1fe)`
Dark: `palette.primary.900 (#00274b)` (unchanged) | Bridge light, color.text.muted on color.bg.zone: 4.64 -> 5.1 AA
Bridge light, color.text.link on color.bg.zone: 7.03 -> 7.74 AAA
Bridge light, focus.ring.color on color.bg.zone: 7.03 -> 7.74 AAA

pr.title: Avatar: replace the Claude logo with a Bridge-drawn agent mark
pr.author: peterbono
pr.body:
## What changed and why

The agent Avatar (`<Avatar kind="agent" brand="claude">`) shipped the Claude logo (simple-icons `siClaude` path and the Anthropic brand color `#D97757`) on a cream tile, inside the published `@bridge-ds/react`. Anthropic's trademark guidelines (anthropic.com/legal/trademark-guidelines, effective 2024-08-01) require prior approval for every use of their logos. Bridge now draws its own agent mark and ships no vendor logo anywhere.

Agent-authored (Claude Code), to be reviewed by the owner before merge. Do not publish to npm without the owner's OK: the release PR changesets opens afterwards stays unmerged.

### The mark

- A prompt chevron and a cursor line, drawn in the Field Guide line style (stroke in `currentColor`, round caps and joins, slightly hand-drawn quadratic curves, no fill). Not a face, not a sparkle, not any company's logo.
- Deep Harbor line (`color.action.primary.bg`, the same role the Field Guide drawings use for "deep") on a Harbor tile. Dark theme: the dark zone tile with the light Deep Harbor line. Contrast = the `action.primary.bg` on `bg.zone` pair the token build already checks (7.03 light, 9.60 dark, ocean 4.81).
- A rounded square (`radius.inset`) instead of a circle, so an agent never reads as a person at a glance, even in a group next to illustrated faces on the same Harbor color (GitHub draws apps and bots the same way).
- Mark box per size on the size scale: 16, 20, 24, 28px for xs, sm, md, lg (line 1.5 to 2.5px).
- Explored six glyphs next to illustrated faces at every size (prompt, drafting divider, node graph, cursor, trail with flag, loop). Rejected: the divider reads as an "A" (too close to an Anthropic monogram), nodes read as "share", cursor reads as Figma, trail and loop are noise at 20px.

### API (non-breaking, minor)

- `kind="agent"` and `brand="claude"` unchanged; the accessible name stays "Claude AI".
- New `AGENT_MARK` export (`viewBox`, `path`, `strokeWidth`, `color`). `CLAUDE_MARK` stays exported as a `@deprecated` alias pointing to `AGENT_MARK`.
- New optional `mark?: ReactNode` (agents only): a vendor logo for teams who have the brand owner's approval. Documented in `Avatar.docs.json` guidance.
- The trademark code comment is rewritten.

### Every place the Claude logo, its color or the cream tile appeared

| Place | Was | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `packages/react/src/components/Avatar/Avatar.tsx` | `CLAUDE_MARK` (siClaude path + `#D97757`), rendered as a fill | `AGENT_MARK` + deprecated alias, drawn mark, `mark` prop, new comment |
| `packages/react/src/components/Avatar/index.ts` | exported `CLAUDE_MARK` | exports `AGENT_MARK` and `CLAUDE_MARK` |
| `packages/react/src/dom/avatar.ts` (`avatarHtml`, used by docs-site `scripts/people.ts`) | Claude path markup | agent mark markup (same as React, tested) |
| `packages/react/src/components/Avatar/Avatar.module.css` | cream tile, circle, mark 62% | Harbor rounded square, Deep Harbor line, sized mark box |
| `packages/tokens/src/semantic/{light,dark}.tokens.json` `color.agent.surface` | `{palette.warning.50}` cream in both themes | `{palette.primary.200}` light, `{palette.primary.900}` dark |
| `packages/tokens/src/brands/ocean.light.tokens.json` | (none) | `color.agent.surface` follows the ocean zone (`primary.50`) |
| `Avatar.docs.json` | "cream" anatomy, Claude mark wording | Bridge mark wording, `mark` guidance sentence, anatomy |
| `Avatar.stories.tsx` | "Claude mark on its cream tile" | Bridge mark; group story now mixes people and the agent at every size |
| `packages/react/component-specs.json` + Figma UI kit | no agent variant (kind "does not change the styles") | Kind axis person/agent, agent variants draw the mark as a vector bound to `color.action.primary.bg`, tile bound to `avatar.agent-bg` |
| `packages/core/src/node/component-specs.ts` | dropped `stroke-linejoin` | keeps it (the mark's chevron joins stay round in Figma) |
| `apps/figma-plugin/test/component-pull.test.ts` | `Size=md, Fallback=initials` | variant name with `Kind=person`, new assertions on the agent variant |
| docs-site uses (`faces.tsx`, `ComponentsList.tsx`, `LibraryEditMode.tsx`, `scripts/people.ts`) | rendered the logo through the Avatar | unchanged code, now render the Bridge mark |

Not found anywhere else: no Claude path in MCP, admin, docs json, snapshots or public assets. The name "Claude AI" is kept everywhere the agent is named.

Note for Figma: the Avatar set gains a `Kind` property. The agent variants exist for both Fallback values (the fallback does not apply to agents), 16 variants instead of 8.

## Risk tier

- [ ] Tier 1, low
- [ ] Tier 2, medium
- [x] Tier 3, high: token value changed (`color.agent.surface`), new prop and export. Design + tech owner approval required

## Authored by

- [ ] Human
- [x] AI agent (Claude), reviewed by a human before merge

## Design review checklist

- [x] Uses tokens only (`npm run lint:css` passes)
- [x] Semantic tokens used in components, not primitives
- [x] Checked in Storybook in **light and dark** themes
- [x] Accessibility: axe tests pass; the mark is decorative, the name is on the root
- [x] Stories updated (sizes, group mixing people and the agent at xs, sm, md, lg)
- [x] Changeset: minor `@bridge-ds/react`, patch tokens, core, figma-plugin
- [x] No lint rule disabled, no test or story deleted

## Checks run locally

typecheck, `npm test` (1708 passed), plugin tests (113 passed), mcp tests (134 passed), lint:css, audit:docs, specs check, build-storybook, docs:build.

## UI quality bar

Component-level change, no new screen. Studio home (light and dark, 1440) checked with real repo data: the agent tile sits in the greeting zone and in the row card; one primary action (Review) unchanged, no change to font sizes or interactive counts (page content and shell unchanged by this PR). Bridge brand: Deep Harbor is the only strong color in the mark, Harbor stays a zone color, no vendor color left.

## Screenshots

Local screenshots (Storybook AllStates and Agent stories, Studio home), light and dark, attached by the agent in its report.

pr.title: Avatar: illustrated faces and Claude's identity; Quality health header with Share
pr.author: peterbono
pr.body:
## What changed and why

Claude Code wrote this PR. The owner pre-approved the design and tech on 2026-10-19, including the new dependency. It is rebased on main after #136 (the new home and the review queue) #140 to #147 (the Branches page with its shared row component, the nav order and Figma coverage), and #150, #152 and #153 (the branch review and the reworked review queue). Do not merge: it waits for the owner.

### 1. DS Avatar (`@bridge-ds/react` minor, `@bridge-ds/tokens` minor)

| API | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `fallback?: 'initials' \| 'illustrated'` (default `initials`) | `illustrated` shows a drawn face when there is no photo, or when the photo fails. The same `seed` always gives the same face. |
| `seed?: string` (default: the name) | Pass the login, so a renamed person keeps their face. |
| `illustration?: string` | A ready image for the illustrated fallback. Without it, `illustrated` shows initials. |
| `kind?: 'person' \| 'agent'` + `brand: 'claude'` | The Claude mark (orange `#D97757`, path from simple-icons `siClaude`) on a cream tile with a hairline edge. Same round shape as people. Accessible name "Claude AI". `name` is optional for the preset. |
| `@bridge-ds/react/avatar-illustrated` (new entry) | `Avatar` (fills `illustration` from the seed), `illustratedAvatarSvg(seed)`, `illustratedAvatarUri(seed)`. |
| `@bridge-ds/react/dom` | `avatarHtml(options)`. Same markup as the React Avatar, with a parity test. |

**How the faces are drawn**
- DiceBear "Notionists" style: design CC0 1.0 by Zoish, code MIT.
- Dependencies `@dicebear/core@9.4.3` and `@dicebear/collection@9.4.3`, pinned.
- Generated locally, no network. Only `notionists` is imported.
- No hands or body icons, and framed on the face (`scale` 125, `translateY` 12) so they read at 20 to 40px.
- The SVG is transparent; the tile colour comes from a token.
- Install note: `@dicebear/collection` also installs the other DiceBear styles, some of them CC BY 4.0. Only the CC0 Notionists drawings reach a bundle. To avoid installing them, `@dicebear/notionists` is a drop-in swap.

**Bundle impact**
- The drawings weigh 381 kB minified, about 122 kB gzipped. They live in the separate `./avatar-illustrated` entry, so the main entry stays light.
- Built package: `dist/index.js` and `dist/dom.js` contain no DiceBear code. `dist/avatar-illustrated.js` is 1.3 kB, plus a shared 5.6 kB Avatar chunk, because DiceBear stays an external dependency.
- The main entry grows by the Avatar code and the Claude path, about 3 kB raw.
- In Studio the drawings load on demand: a dynamic import after the first paint, as one 381 kB chunk. Pages that show no people never load them. The static Library examples draw at build time and ship no JavaScript.

**Tokens (tier 3, pre-approved)**
- `color.illustration.surface`: light is `palette.primary.200` (the Harbor zone colour). Dark is `palette.primary.300`, because the navy dark zone made the black lines vanish. Black lines are 16.6:1 on the light value and 13.4:1 on the dark one.
- `avatar.illustrated-bg` points to `color.illustration.surface`.
- `color.agent.surface` is `palette.warning.50`, cream, the same in both themes. `avatar.agent-bg` and `avatar.agent-border` (`color.border.default`) go with it.
- Contrast note: the Claude orange on the cream tile is 2.91:1. The mark is a decorative logo inside an element named "Claude AI", so it adds no contrast pair. `contrast.checks.json` is untouched.

**Docs and tests**
- Stories: Illustrated and Agent, plus `AllStates` rows for every size, a broken image, and a group mixing people and Claude.
- `Avatar.docs.json`: the Library examples draw at build time.
- Tests: the same seed gives the same face and a different seed a different one; the main entry falls back to initials; a failing image falls back to the drawing; the Claude preset has its accessible name, passes axe, and can be decorative; the `+N` counter names agents; the DOM renderer matches the React markup.
- Changeset: react minor, tokens minor, docs-site minor.

**Trademark:** the Claude logo is an Anthropic trademark, used here only to attribute actions Claude took. **The owner must check Anthropic's brand guidelines before release.**

### 2. Adoption in Studio

Faces and display names, through `scripts/people.ts`, `lib/people.ts` and `components/ds/studio/faces.ts`.

**Display names**
- Shown instead of "@login": in the change and history details, the conversation line, explorations, the history author filter, the release card ("can publish it"), and the who-acts sentences of a change (`markLogins`).
- Names come from the GitHub profile (`GET /users/:login`), cached for a week.
- Lookups per page view: 4 when anonymous, 20 when signed in. The viewer's own name comes free.
- With no profile name, the login shows without "@". No name is invented (peterbono has none).

**Faces** (the illustrated face, seeded by login, wherever there was no photo)
- Change rows, with ", by <name>" for screen readers.
- History rows and the history detail byline.
- Explorations.
- The new home: the "waiting on you" stack, the Needs you rows, and the reviewer on branch cards. This also removes the 12px and 10.5px initials font sizes on the home.
- The review queue, through the shared row component.
- Places that already showed a GitHub photo keep it: the change header and the conversation.

**Claude's identity**
- Shown on: Claude-made changes (`agentMade`: labels, body markers, Co-Authored-By), which read "Claude, with <name>"; history entries; explorations; the home "Claude AI" rows and stack; guidance drafts in Components ("Draft by Claude, needs review" with the mark in front); and the Library edit mode flags ("Drafted by Claude", "Claude proposes").

**Shared files touched (minimal edits)**
- `lib/changes.ts`: `CachedPull.agent`.
- `styles/site.css`: `.person`.
- `scripts/reviews.ts`, `scripts/history/page.ts`, `StudioHome.tsx`.

**Two fixes found on the way**
- History crashed ("Cannot read properties of null (reading 'value')"): the DS Input ignores `id`, so `#hs-token` never existed. The page now finds the field by its datalist.
- The history detail showed the "Next release" zone (two Harbor zones) and a raw commit title. It now has one zone and the full human title (`historySummary(e, { full: true })`).

### 3. Quality page

**Header**
- Title with Share at the end of the title line, at both widths.
- One Harbor zone holding:
  - a verdict that names the single open finding: "Nothing blocks the library. VisuallyHidden guidance is a draft."
  - one primary, "Review guidance", full width on phones.
  - the three Library health cards, each linking to its section below: 0 failing contrast checks (304 checked in 2 brands, light and dark), 97.8% of components come from Bridge (up from 7.6%), and 52 of 53 components have reviewed guidance (1 drafted by Claude).
- Every number comes from the contrast gate (`lib/stats`), the committed audit reports and the guidance state. The page reads them through `lib/library-health.ts`, which has tests.

**Share** (a secondary button opening a DS Menu)
- Copy summary: copies the text below and announces "Summary copied. Paste it in Slack or on a slide.":
  ```
  Bridge library health
  Nothing blocks the library. VisuallyHidden guidance is a draft.

  - All 304 contrast checks pass in 2 brands, light and dark.
  - 97.8% of components in 2 products come from Bridge, up from 7.6% before Bridge.
  - 52 of 53 components have reviewed usage guidance: 1 drafted by Claude to review.

  Details: <origin>/studio/quality/
  ```
- Download image: `bridge-quality.png`, 1200x630 at 2x. It is an SVG built from the same numbers, with colours read from the page tokens (so it follows light or dark) and the page's latin Fraunces and Instrument Sans embedded. It is drawn on a canvas client side, with no new dependency. Verified in headless Chrome in both themes.


### After the #147 rebase

- **Shared row:** home and Branches now draw people through one shared `Who` (`components/ds/studio/faces.tsx`), used by both StudioHome and BranchesList as the `BranchRow` `who`. Both show the illustrated face when there is no photo, and Claude's identity on Claude-made work.
- **Display-name rule** (`lib/home-model` `shortName`, used by `displayName` and the greeting):
  - Use the first word of the GitHub profile name, unless it is an article (The, A, An, Le, La, Les) or shorter than 2 letters.
  - In that case use the full name ("The Octocat", "J. Doe"). With no profile name, use the login.
  - Unit tested.
- **Props shape:** `AvatarProps` is one interface again, so the docs tables and the Figma spec reader can read it. The component itself keeps the strict `AvatarPersonProps | AvatarAgentProps` type.
- **Component specs:** `component-specs.json` is regenerated. Avatar gains a Fallback axis. Its preview text now reads "?" instead of "FG", because the reader cannot evaluate the agent name fallback.


### Shared branch row (owner feedback, 2026-10-20)

`BranchRow` is used by the home Needs you list, the review queue and Branches.

- **Two fixed lines on every row:**
  - Line 1 is the title alone, on one line with an ellipsis. The full title is in the link's `title` attribute.
  - Line 2 is the optional Jira key in mono, the muted sentence, then the status pill right after it.
  - The " · " separator is gone.
- **Phones (390):** the sentence may wrap and the pill may go under it, inside the text block. The row button stays at the end, never between.
- **Rows without a person** (health, setup): the icon sits in the avatar's box, 32px round, on the initials avatar tile (`--avatar-bg`). It uses a plain glyph (TriangleAlert, Check) so it never draws a circle inside a circle, and the leading column aligns.
- **Screenshots:** a row with a long title, light and dark, at 1440, 1920 and 390: `it6-*` and `it7-*`.
- **Figma plugin test:** it now addresses the Avatar variant as `Size=md, Fallback=initials`, since the spec has the new Fallback axis.


### After the #152 rebase

- **Branch review (`BranchReview`):** the "who asks" header and every conversation entry draw people through the shared `Who`. That means the GitHub photo, else the illustrated face, and Claude as Claude, with names from the review's display-name map (never logins).
- **Review queue list:** each item shows the face of who waits on you (person or Claude) between the progress mark and the title.
- **Unchanged from main:** `scripts/reviews.ts` and `review-queue.css` keep main's new structure. My older string-built detail adoption was dropped with them, because main's React review replaced it.

### UI bar

- Screenshots: `scratchpad/avatar-quality/`, light and dark, 1440 and 390, iterations it1 to it4.
- Interactive elements on the first screen (page content / with shell):

  | Page | 1440 | 390 |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | Quality | about 12 / 25 | 6 / 12 |
  | Home | 8 / 23 | 4 / 8 |
  | Review queue | 5 / 20 | 6 / 10 |
  | History | 13 / 24 | 9 / 13 |
  | Explorations | 8 / 19 | 4 / 8 |
  | Components | 25 / 38 | 13 / 19 |
  | Changes, Merged filter | 27 / 38 | 24 / 28 |

  - Quality at 1440: the automatic count says 35 / 48, but that includes 23 hidden links of the footer "View source" menu.
  - Components and Changes are long lists: the count is mostly the rows themselves.
- Font sizes on the first screen: 3 or 4 everywhere. One exception: on Quality the existing AdoptionMetric value (21px) peeks in at the bottom of 1440.
- One Harbor zone per screen, one primary per view. No horizontal scroll at 390.
- No em dash, and no developer words added on first screens.

### Critique iterations (subagent critic)

1. **Iteration 1** found:
   - faces vanishing on the dark zone;
   - two Harbor zones and a commit title on the history detail;
   - the person and date misaligned;
   - the Claude tile with no edge on white;
   - the Claude mark detached from its pill;
   - Share alone on its line at 390;
   - the lone primary not filling its bar;
   - a verdict that did not name the finding.

   All fixed (new token step, `.cg-who`, `cm-flag`, mobile header).
2. **Iteration 2** found:
   - the Components table overflowing at 390;
   - two wordings for one action;
   - a summary repeating the title;
   - a small byline avatar.

   All fixed.
3. **Iteration 3** found the history heading cut at 90 characters. Fixed with the full title option.
4. **After the #136 rebase:** home and review queue adopted and shot signed in, through the read-only proxy.

### Not done, and why

- **One face per person everywhere:** list rows draw faces because list data has no photos. Details keep the photos they already showed.
- **Out of scope:** "#123" and "Open on GitHub" in rows, the sidebar "Connect GitHub" primary, and the history token table layout. They exist on main and are owned elsewhere.
- **DS request:** `Input` ignores a passed `id` inside its Field, so `<Input id>` cannot be found by id. Worked around in the page; it needs a fix in the DS.

## Risk tier

- [ ] Tier 1, low
- [ ] Tier 2, medium
- [x] Tier 3, high: tokens added, new dependency, new package entry. Pre-approved by the owner (design and tech).

## Authored by

- [ ] Human
- [x] AI agent (Claude), reviewed by a human before merge

## Design review checklist

- [x] Uses tokens only (`npm run lint:css` passes); the Claude orange is part of the brand mark SVG, not CSS
- [x] Semantic or component tokens in components
- [x] Checked in light and dark
- [x] Axe checks in tests, visible focus unchanged
- [x] Stories for every new state
- [x] Changeset added (react minor, tokens minor, docs-site minor)
- [x] No lint rule disabled, no test or story deleted

Checks run locally after the last rebase: typecheck, npm test (1682 tests), lint:css, audit:docs (100%, no allowlist), docs:build, build-storybook, build:packages (react), plugin:test, mcp:test, bridge check.

pr.body:
## What changed and why

Dark mode polish and the leftovers from the earlier critiques. Agent-authored (Claude), design and tech pre-approved by the owner. Every number on screen still comes from GitHub or repo data.

### Asked fixes
1. **SegmentedControl, dark:** the selected segment's edge is `color.control.checked.bg`, the same edge as a pressed Button toggle (#118). Before, `border.default` matched the raised plate in dark, so there was no edge. The edge also shows in light (Deep Harbor on the white plate), which matches the Button toggle.
2. **Banner strong, dark:** new semantic `color.surface.strong` (`palette.primary.700` in both themes, so Deep Harbor). It replaces `action.primary.bg`, which is light blue in dark and read like a Harbor zone. Text and focus ring use `color.text.on-solid` (8.87:1 bridge, 7.39:1 ocean).
3. **Owner override confirmation** (scripts/reviews.ts): the native `<dialog>` is gone. It is now a `ScriptDialog` (the `dialogHtml` / `openDialog` / `closeDialog` from `@bridge-ds/react/dom`, #127) in `pages/studio/changes.astro`, using DS Textarea, Alert, ButtonGroup and SegmentedControl.
   - The script fills in the change number, the approvals it skips and the allowed merge methods.
   - Listeners are replaced through an AbortController on each repaint, so they never stack.
   - The merge method sits in a "For developers" fold, as a DS SegmentedControl. A DS Select can't be used: its portaled popup would be inert under the modal.
   - A reason that is too short shows its message in the field hint, with `aria-invalid`. The Alert is only for GitHub errors.
   - The copy says "ship", not "merge".
4. **All tokens:** the filter Input and the type SegmentedControl are both `md` (44px). A small SegmentedControl is 38px, against 32px for a small Input. The filter field is now full width on phones.
5. **Quality audit tables:** `narrowLayout="stack"` on the four report tables and on ContrastFailTable, with a `label` on each cell because the page is static. The `ad-scroll` wrappers are removed.

### Earlier critic findings, checked on main
- **Neutral Badge and grey status chips losing their fill in dark: fixed.** New `color.feedback.neutral.bg` (neutral.100 light, neutral.800 dark). `bg.subtle` is the card color in dark.
- **Combobox list barely separated from a Dialog in dark: fixed.** The `popup.border` component token is now `color.border.emphasis` (neutral.700 in dark). This applies to every popup.
- **Changes tab bar scrolling on phones: fixed.** The tab reads "All" at 480px and below, and the four tabs fit at 390.
- **Tokens filter chips with a near-black fill: fixed.** The selected chip uses `surface.selected` with the checked edge.
- **"Changed in this change" repeated on every row: fixed.** It is now "Changed", "New" or "Changed, dark theme only", since the banner already names the change.
- **Oversized "Bring in the latest library": fixed.** It was the DS `lg` (48px) and is now `md` (44px), the same as the other row actions.
- **"Your turn: fix tests": fixed.** The logic was wrong. The list chip told a designer author it was their turn, while the detail page said "Waiting for a developer… Your design is not the problem".
  - A new pure helper, `developerOnlyFailures` (lib/check-explain), classifies failing check names.
  - `whoActs` now gives developer-only failures to "a developer", with the chip "Blocked by tests". This applies to the list and the Overview.
  - A failing design rule stays the author's turn. Unit tests are added.
- **"N updates behind": fixed.** It now reads "Library moved on: N updates".
- **Native select in the Tokens Options sheet: already gone on main.** It is a BridgedSelect. Checked in the DOM: 0 `select`, 1 DS combobox.
- **Search palette result icon: fixed.** The colored chart-series dots are replaced by the side nav's DS Icons (page, component, token). Color tokens keep their swatch.
- **Studio overview hero action: kept, it meets the bar.** "Start a change" is a secondary Menu on the page title line (the page header action), with one primary in the to-do rows. At 390 it fills its bar.

A static page can set `aria-invalid` (red border) and write the message into the hint, but the hint doesn't turn to the error color. Component request: a `data-error` hook, or a `fieldErrorHtml` helper in `@bridge-ds/react/dom`.

- **Critic notes outside this scope, for follow-ups:**

pr.title: Brand: Field Guide direction for Bridge (tokens, DS, site)
pr.author: peterbono
pr.body:
## What changed and why

Applies brand direction B "Field Guide" (the owner's pick, "more restful", exactly as mocked) to the design system and to the Bridge site, which is built with it. Agent-authored (Claude Code), to be reviewed by a human before merge.

**Tokens (Tier 3, owner-approved), `@bridge-ds/tokens` major**
- New `color.ink` and `color.harbor` ramps, generated in OKLCH like the others, with the brand hexes pinned in `scripts/ramps.mjs`: ink 900 `#15202B`, 600 `#5B6672`, 200 `#E3E8EE`; Harbor 200 `#CFE8FF`; Deep Harbor 700 `#0B4A8B`.
- In the bridge brand, neutral now maps to ink, and primary, accent and link map to harbor. Info moves to plum and the categorical chart hue to orange.
- `color.bg.default` is now white. A new `color.bg.zone` holds the large Harbor blocks (dark: a muted deep blue).
- Deep Harbor now drives primary actions, checked controls, links and focus. Dark mode uses a lighter Harbor (`harbor.300`) with `harbor.950` text.
- Ocean keeps its tinted canvas, its sea links and a paler zone through its override file.
- Type: Fraunces for display and headings, Instrument Sans for body and UI, Plex Mono for code. They come through `font.family.display` and `font.family.sans` plus new `typography.<display|h1|h2|h3|body|ui|caption>.*` roles in both brands. New `font.leading.*` values; a few `font.size` steps move to the B scale (16, 21, 30, 36, 44, 64).
- Radius roles in bridge: 6 / 12 / 20 / 20 / pill (primitive `radius.xl` is now 12). Default controls are 44px, compact ones 36px (new `size.11`).
- Contrast gate: 296 checks, 0 failing, including 5 new pairs on `color.bg.zone`. The tightest bridge pair is muted text on the zone, at 4.64:1.

**React (`@bridge-ds/react` patch)**
- PageHeader, Card, Dialog and Drawer titles read the typography roles.
- Badge md is 14/20, to match the B chips.
- No API change.

**Bridge site (`apps/docs-site`)**
- Top bar has 5 items: logo, Library | Studio, search, theme, GitHub or the account avatar.
- Side nav:
  - At most 7 entries, no group headings and no counts. Groups are buttons with `aria-expanded`, and only the current group opens. Drafts is the one badge.
  - Library: Home, Foundations, Tokens, Components, Use. Studio: Overview, Tokens, Components, Changes, Quality, Settings. Settings joins the Studio space.
- Things that moved:
  - Version chip: next to the page title.
  - Branch picker: next to the Studio title.
  - Brand and density: into the preview toolbars (foundations pages, component previews).
- The theme playground is removed, and `/playground/` redirects to the Library home.
- Library home and Studio overview follow `b-home` / `b-studio`, all with real data:
  - "Hello Florian." appears only when a GitHub login is known.
  - The review count, the status sentence and the "Unblock" suggestion come from open PRs and their live CI and review status.
  - "Add usage guidance" lists the components that really have no docs.
  - The contrast line comes from the build.
- Every Library section page opens with a Harbor header block. The Color page follows `b-color`.
- The illustrations are reused exactly as mocked. They are painted with tokens (strokes `currentColor`, fills `data-fill`), so they follow dark mode, and they are kept as placeholders.
- Every font size in the site CSS now reads a typography role. `.stylelintrc.json` additionally accepts `var(--typography-<role>-family)` for `font-family` (still tokens only).
- Docs: `docs/DESIGN-LANGUAGE.md` (v2) and `apps/docs-site/DESIGN.md` describe the new direction.

**Admin demo:** it changed only through tokens; no admin CSS was edited. It builds and looks coherent: white canvas, Instrument Sans, Deep Harbor links and chart.

| Library home 1440 | 16 | 4 (64, 21, 16, 14) | none |

## Checks run locally

`tokens:build` (296 contrast checks, 0 failing), `typecheck`, `lint:css`, `npm test` (443 tests), `mcp:test` (68), `plugin:test` (13), `build-storybook`, `docs:build`, `admin:build`, `audit:docs` (100% tokens, 100% components, no regression). Visual impact runs in CI on this PR.

## Open issues

- The Studio token explorer still mixes 6 sizes: the DS Kbd at 11.9 and 13.6px, and dense rows. Its compact 36px toolbar pass is not done yet.
- On Settings pages, the DS Table header (12px) makes a 5th size.
- The GitHub avatar shows only after connecting; before that the top bar shows "Connect GitHub".
- `color.bg.zone` reads "Unused" in component usage: only the site uses it.
- The steel and cable primitive ramps are kept for consumers, but no brand uses them.

## Risk tier

- [ ] Tier 2, medium
- [x] Tier 3, high: token values and roles changed, `.stylelintrc.json` touched. Design and tech owner approval required

pr.title: Bridge on Bridge: the docs app built with the design system it documents
pr.author: peterbono
pr.body:
## What changed and why

Bridge, the docs platform (`apps/docs-site`), is now built with the Bridge design system it documents (dogfooding). Agent-authored (Claude Code, lead agent plus parallel sub-agents on disjoint files), reviewed by nobody yet.

- **Tokens.** The chrome palette (Fog, Deck, Steel, Slate, International Orange, Cable) was the DS `bridge` brand with drifted values, so no third brand was needed. Every `--br-*` variable now maps to a DS semantic token (`color.*`, `font.*`, radius roles, `elevation.*`, `motion.*`, `layer.*`), and `src/brand/tokens.ts` is removed. `<html>` is pinned to `data-brand="bridge"` and comfortable density. The scope menu only reaches preview surfaces (`data-preview-brand` / `data-preview-density`).
- **New tokens (Tier 3, owner asked).** These are DTCG, in both themes, with descriptions and a changeset:
  - `color.chart.series.1-6`, `color.chart.track`, `color.chart.grid` and `color.chart.axis`, on a new `palette.categorical` role (bridge: plum, ocean: orange).
  - `color.border.emphasis`.
  - `layout.sidebar.width`, `layout.header.height` and `layout.content.max-width`.
  - `size.40` and `size.64`.
  - `font.size.900` and `font.size.1000`, for landing display only.
  - The chart pairs join the contrast gate: 276 checks, all brands and themes pass.
- **CSS.** All 20 docs stylesheets pass the same token-only stylelint rules as component CSS (the docs-site exemption is gone), plus `bridge/use-tokens`. 141 rules made dead by the swap are deleted. Global `kbd`, `table` and link rules no longer hit DS parts.
- **Components.** Controls render with `@bridge-ds/react`, statically by default; the vanilla scripts keep their id and `data-*` hooks. The components used are Button, IconButton, ButtonLink, Badge, Tag, Kbd, Alert, EmptyState, Input, Textarea, Select, Switch, Table, Breadcrumb, Link, Popover (the scope and version menus, `client:idle`) and the two new ones below.
- **New DS components (Tier 2).** Both are reused 3+ times and come with stories, `docs.json` and tests:
  - `SegmentedControl` (Forms) has a static HTML contract that a vanilla script can drive.
  - `PageHeader` (Layout).
- **Audit fixes (`@bridge-ds/core`, patch).**
  - A ring built only from tokens (`inset 0 0 0 var() var()`) is no longer counted as a hardcoded shadow.
  - `<Button render={<a href />}>` no longer counts the anchor as a separate native link.
- **Enforcement.** `lint:css` builds and runs `@bridge-ds/stylelint-plugin` on docs-site CSS. `npm run audit:docs`, in the CI docs job, runs `bridge audit apps/docs-site/src --baseline bridge-site-after.json --no-regress --fail-under 95`. I checked locally that both fail on an injected raw value.
- **Adoption page.** Two apps sit side by side, each showing before and after: "Admin demo (react-admin, migrated from MUI)" (untouched) and "Bridge itself (dogfooding)". Each app has its own trend.

### Audit, Bridge docs site

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Token adoption | 9.7% (281 refs, 2628 hardcoded, 1932 `--br-*` refs) | 99.96%, shown as 100% (4667 refs, 2 hardcoded) |
| Component adoption | 52.8% (47 of 89) | 100% (210 of 210 scanned instances) |

The audit does not tell the whole story:
- **The 2 hardcoded values left** are `#000000` defaults of the color-picker `<input type="color">` in the token editor scripts. They are data, not styling.
- **The audit only reads CSS, TS and TSX.** Astro templates and HTML strings built by scripts are not scanned. Native controls in `.astro` files went from 178 to about 60, mostly `details` disclosures, the palette `dialog`, range and checkbox inputs, and selects filled by scripts. innerHTML templates in `src/scripts` still hold about 76 native elements: Reviews, History, the explorer detail panel and inline edit. These are listed in `apps/admin/DS-GAPS.md`, and the Adoption page says it in the Bridge card.

## Risk tier

- [ ] Tier 1, low: docs, stories, lint or a11y fixes, no visual or API change
- [x] Tier 2, medium: new component, variant or prop (additive). Opened as draft until design review
- [x] Tier 3, high: token added/changed/removed, breaking API, or guardrail change. Design + tech owner approval required

This PR also touches guardrails: `.stylelintrc.json`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, and `contrast.checks.json` (pairs added, none loosened). The owner requested these changes.

## Authored by

- [ ] Human
- [x] AI agent (Claude), reviewed by a human before merge

## Design review checklist

- [x] Uses tokens only: no hex, rgb, hsl or raw shadows in component CSS (`npm run lint:css` passes)
- [x] Semantic tokens used in components, not primitives, for color and elevation
- [ ] Checked in Storybook in **light and dark** themes: Storybook builds; the new stories were not reviewed by eye
- [x] Accessibility: the axe checks in the SegmentedControl test pass
- [x] Stories added or updated for every new state
- [x] Changeset added with the right bump (`patch` / `minor` / `major`)
- [x] No lint rule disabled, no test or story deleted. Four count assertions were updated to the new truth: 276 contrast checks and 48 components; the contrast cell now ends with "and N more".

## Checks run locally

tokens:build, typecheck, lint:css, npm test (440), mcp:test (68), plugin:test, docs:build, admin:build, build-storybook and audit:docs all pass.

## Visual QA

Before is production, after is the local build. Shots cover Home, Color, Button, Studio overview, Studio tokens and Reviews, in light and dark at 1440, plus Home and Tokens at 390. Expected visual differences:
- **Shape:** tighter radii (cards 14 to 10, hero 20 to 14, controls 10 to 6).
- **Color:** a slightly bluer Fog canvas.
- **Type:** UI text is 14 px instead of 15.
- **Hero:** the orange radial washes are gone (DS: solid surfaces only), and the title tops out at 60 px instead of 68.
- **Charts and KPIs:** values sit on the scale, e.g. 42 instead of 40.
- **Top bar:** new key caps.

Fixed during QA:
- The hamburger showed on desktop.
- 390 px had a horizontal scroll.
- The hero icons had been lost.

Click-tested by script: theme toggle, Cmd K palette, scope menu (the preview brand changes, the chrome stays bridge), explorer lens and arrow keys, and the mobile rail.

## Open issues

- **The Studio "Health" card now lists 15 semantic tokens as not in use.** It only counts library component CSS, so app-level tokens (chart, layout, border emphasis) look unused.
- **Global `li + li` and heading margins in `site.css` can still reach DS lists and headings** (Breadcrumb, SidebarNav, PageHeader). Nothing showed in the QA shots.
- **DS gaps still open:**
  - A static mode (no hydration) for Tabs, Accordion, Switch, Select and Slider.
  - `Field` drops the `id` you pass.
  - `[hidden]` is beaten by module `display`.
  - No pressed or toggle Button.
  - A row-header `TableCell` prop.
  - Brand icons.
  - A `Stat` component (only 2 uses).
  - `color.chart.area`.
- **The scope and version menus now ship React on every page** (two `client:idle` islands).

pr.title: Bridge v1: design system as code, web platform, Figma plugin, MCP and CLI
pr.author: peterbono
pr.body:
## Bridge v1: design system as code, end to end

Agent-authored integration of all Bridge work (Claude Code). **Risk tier 3**: adds and restructures tokens, renames packages to `@bridge-ds/*`, touches `.github/`. Needs design and tech review. Humans merge.

### What's in it
- **Design system**: tiered DTCG tokens (primitives, brands bridge/ocean, semantic light/dark, density, components), contrast gate (220 checks, 0 failing), 46 React components on Base UI, design language doc, Vitest + axe tests.
- **Bridge web platform** (`apps/docs-site`): token explorer with editing (every edit becomes a PR), Reviews (approve, request changes, merge with governance rules), History with revert planner, Branches, Adoption, Connect your Claude (MCP).
- **DS Bridge Figma plugin**: Pull (code to Figma) and Push (Figma to PR), tiered collections, contrast column fixed (the bug seen on #4).
- **MCP server + CLI** (`@bridge-ds/mcp`, `@bridge-ds/cli`): 21 tools for the user's own Claude, read-only without a token, never pushes to main.
- **Visual impact**: before/after/diff screenshots of impacted stories and app screens, posted on PRs.
- **Adoption audit**: `bridge audit`, Stylelint and ESLint plugins.
- **Branch previews**: snapshot packages per PR (pkg.pr.new), Vercel configs, staging token override. One-time setup in `docs/PREVIEWS.md`.
- **Demo product** (`apps/admin`): react-admin e-commerce demo (MIT, credited) migrated from MUI to Bridge, two fictional shops. Audit: tokens 0% to 100%, components 0% to 90.2% (remaining gaps listed in `apps/admin/DS-GAPS.md`).

### Checks run locally
tokens:build, typecheck, lint:css, admin:lint:css, npm test (327), mcp:test (68), plugin test (13) + build, plugins:build, build:packages (8), admin build, build-storybook, docs:build, `bridge check`, MCP stdio smoke test.

### Reviewer focus
- `.github/workflows/*` (new jobs: visual impact, preview packages, release which is inert without `NPM_TOKEN`).
- Package scope rename `@bridge-ds/*` (not published yet).
- Badge default is now subtle; Tooltip has no `role="tooltip"` (Base UI 1.9 behaviour).

### Not done / known limits
- Web write actions (approve, merge, propose) not yet exercised against GitHub.
- Overlay component previews in docs show only the trigger.
- Packages not published on npm; previews need the setup in `docs/PREVIEWS.md`.

Each ships built ES modules, type declarations and, for React, one `styles.css`; the monorepo keeps resolving TypeScript sources through the `source` export condition. `@bridge-ds/core` adds branch preview helpers (`previewUrl`, `snapshotUrl`, `previewComment`) and a `previews` section in `bridge.config.json`. `@bridge-ds/react` adds an opt-in staging token override: `ThemeProvider` `tokenOverride` loads an allowlisted `tokens.css` from `?bridge-tokens=`, off by default and refused in production builds unless enabled.

Data display: Card restyled as a flat plate with an `interactive` option and padding sizes; Badge gains `appearance` (subtle, now the default, or solid), a dot, icons and sizes (existing solid badges must pass `appearance="solid"` to keep their look); new Avatar and AvatarGroup, Table (sortable headers with aria-sort, selectable rows, sticky header, focusable scroll region, useTableSort), Accordion, Tag (removable, toggleable), Divider and Kbd. Adds avatar, tag, kbd, divider and accordion component tokens.

Feedback: Alert (five tones, actions, dismiss, correct live region), Toast (ToastProvider and useToast with success, error, warning, info, promise, update and close), Progress (linear and circular, determinate and indeterminate), Skeleton, EmptyState, plus Spinner stories and guidance. Adds alert and skeleton component tokens.

Overlays: Dialog (sizes, scrolling body, footer, close last in focus order), AlertDialog (destructive confirmations, async confirm), Drawer (start, end, bottom with swipe), Popover, Tooltip with TooltipProvider, Menu (icons, shortcuts, groups, submenus, checkbox and radio items, danger items). Every popup carries the theme, brand and density scope. Adds menu and drawer component tokens.

Bridge token system v1. Adds a brand mapping layer (`bridge` default, `ocean` alternate) between primitives and semantic tokens, a component tier (button, input, checkbox, switch, slider, card, popup, dialog, tooltip, toast, table, tabs, progress, nav), comfortable and compact density, motion durations and easings with a reduced-motion override, layers (z-index), icon sizes, breakpoints, a 1.2 type scale from 14px with tracking tokens, and self-hosted IBM Plex Sans and Mono (`@bridge-ds/tokens/fonts.css`). Primitives are regenerated in OKLCH on one lightness ladder. The build now writes `dist/resolved.json` and fails when any pair in `contrast.checks.json` drops below its WCAG minimum in any brand and theme. Fixes `color.border.strong` against `color.surface.default` (now at least 3:1 in both themes).
Add usage guidance files for Button, Input, Badge and Card, plus the list of color pairs to check for contrast. They feed the new documentation site; no visual or API change.

body.body:
## New variant request for Select

Studio's request form is static markup with vanilla scripts, so the DS Select (a React component that needs hydration) cannot be used there; the Kind field stays a plain native select (PR #79). A native appearance of Select (a styled <select> with DS tokens, focus ring, sizes, invalid and disabled states, usable from plain HTML via a class or a tiny web component) would let static pages stay 100% DS. body.title: Spec: Your face, optional drawn-avatar customizer with team-unique Shuffle
body.body:
Draft, docs only (`docs/specs/`). Agent-authored. Risk tier: none (no code); the spec itself flags one Tier 2 (Avatar `xl`) and one optional Tier 3 (tints).

## What this proposes

An optional **Your face** band in Settings > You: one quiet row (your face at 40px + **Change**), opening in place to an 80px preview, **Next to your team** (you and every teammate at 24px), **Shuffle**, and on demand **Pick the parts yourself** (Hair, Glasses, Beard, Expression). Shortcut: "Change your face" in the account menu.

**Uniqueness rule (measured).** At 20px, identity is the hair: hair changes the drawing 0.064, beard and glasses 0.007, eyes/brows/nose/lips 0.001 to 0.002. So within a team a hair style is worn by one person (hard rule, server 409 `face_taken`), and Shuffle also avoids 20px look-alikes (45 measured pairs of 2,016). Whole-face pixel distance alone fails: Dana vs the old Malik drawing measures farther apart than Dana vs Ann. New members get an automatic distinct drawing (`seed#n`), which generalises tonight's `FACE_DRAWING_SEEDS` so nobody writes an exception again. First claim wins across teams; Shuffle avoids taken styles of every team you are in.

**Storage.** A small recipe (part names) on the Bridge account (`POST /api/account { action: 'face' }`, like `aiTools`), plus a per-team face map (`bridge:team:faces:<repo>`) returned by the team read, so `drawFace(seed)` resolves it on every surface. Photo wins over drawing; sample team and no-account sessions keep it in the browser.

**Phases.** P0 no UI (recipe, team map, automatic distinct faces, nightly zero-identical check) fixes the collision alone; P1 row + Shuffle; P2 part pickers + taken states + menu shortcut; P3 photo/drawing choice, tints, phone.

Eight open questions for the founder are in section 14.

## Screens (desktop, 1389x868 @2x, real Bridge Library 1.8.6 + real face drawer)

body.title: Sample team: Add a product for Dana, run in this browser
body.body:
## What changed and why

Owner question (2026-11-13): "why, when I click Start an exploration, is the path to add a new product no longer available?" On the sample team (acme-design-demo/bridge-demo-ds) "Add a product" only showed for a GitHub admin or lead (`useCanAddProduct` / `canAddProduct`), and the sample visitor never is one, even when they "See it as" Dana. Agent-authored (Claude Code).

**Who sees it.** On the sample team, the person played in "See it as" when they run the team: Dana (admin and lead), via the new pure rule `canAddSampleProduct` (lib/add-product.ts) on the played member (`currentContributor`, lib/demo-cast `playedMember`). Sofia and Leo (designers), Ann (product manager) and Malik (developer, no email membership) never see it, as on a real team. Real teams keep the exact old rule.

**Where.** Everywhere AddProduct shows for an admin: Start an exploration's Where list (last option after the separator), Settings > Products on the team shell (TeamProducts), All products. Same dialog, validated board "Add a product v3", not redesigned.

**What runs in this browser.** "add a product" joins `SAMPLE_IN_BROWSER` (lib/demo.ts) with a dialog line in `ACTION_LINES`. Submitting keeps the entry with `keepSampleProduct` (lib/demo-in-browser.ts) under `bridge.acme-design-demo/bridge-demo-ds.draft.products` in localStorage: same storage, same lifetime and same reset as the in-browser starts (`swapDemoDrafts` drops it when the visitor leaves the sample team). `addedHere` (scripts/repo-context.ts) merges it into the team's settings on the sample team only, so the side nav "Products", the product page and the Where list read it. Nothing is sent: no `addToTeam`, no GitHub reads, no POST (tests stub fetch and assert no write call).

**Sample-friendly steps (what I decided).**
- "Its code is on GitHub": no account is read on the sample team, and the card is not marked Recommended there ("Only its address" is). The step shows one drawing and one line, `sampleFoundLine` in lib/add-product.ts, built from the card labels ("On the sample team, Bridge does not look for code on an account. Try Only its address or It's a new product."), with Back only. No Find it on GitHub, no owners' request.
- A product added in this browser shows no "One step before the first preview" setup step on its page (nothing exists to connect).
- "Only its address" and "It's a new product": same form, no code started on GitHub, no linking, no pending-action. The entry keeps only key, name and address (no repo, no designers' copy, no previews).
- "Give designers their own copy" is hidden on the sample team: nothing would be copied. No copy-access or previews step.
- The form's status line says it once, before submitting: `DEMO_WORDS.sampleProduct`, "On the sample team it stays in this browser."
- After adding from Settings, its page opens (as before). After adding from Start an exploration, on every team (real teams too, as StartExploration's header promises), the person comes back to Start with the new product picked: AddProduct's new `onAdded(key)` replaces opening the page there, and the product is known at once (`noteAddedProduct` / `addedHere`). "Sent for review" still shows only for a reviewed add.

**Fix, also on main (real teams): the dialog never finished closing.** Closing Add a product from a form step (It's a new product, Only its address), by Escape or after adding from Start, reset the step to the first question during Base UI's exit. The form step is its own component (StartNewProduct), so the popup remounted mid-exit, the exit never completed, and its see-through backdrop (pointer-events auto) stayed over the page: nothing was clickable. Same code on main, so real teams had it from Settings too. Now the step (and the review step) stays as it is while closing, and each new opening starts from the question (reset before paint). Back from a step also puts the focus on its card again (Base UI's trap had moved it to the popup). Test: "Add a product closes cleanly from every step" (fails on the old code, popup and backdrop still mounted).

**Tests.** demo.test.ts (action line), demo-in-browser.test.ts (runsInBrowser, keep/replace/drop on leaving, broken copies, voice), add-product.test.ts (canAddSampleProduct over the whole cast), AddProduct.test.ts (Dana sees it; GitHub card reads nothing; address path adds in browser, opens its page, no addToTeam, no write; from Start hands back the key; Sofia sees nothing), StartExploration.test.ts (Dana adds "Atlas" from Where: comes back picked, no write, shows in ProductsNav; Sofia, Leo, Ann and Malik don't see it; real-team email admin still doesn't; real team with the add API stubbed: added from Where, back to Start with it picked, its page not opened). `npx tsc -p apps/docs-site --noEmit` is clean on touched files (one pre-existing ListFilters error). No CSS touched. No headless browser on this machine: visual gate still to do.

- [ ] Tier 2, medium: new component, variant or prop (additive). Opened as draft until design review
- [ ] Tier 3, high: token added/changed/removed, breaking API, or guardrail change. Design + tech owner approval required

body.title: Studio search: explorations, review pieces, build requests, products and pages
body.body:
## What changed and why

Owner-approved scope (Florian, 2026-11-13). Studio's header search (Cmd+K) only found components and tokens; it now finds the team's work too, grouped by kind in this order (DS Combobox groups, the heading names the kind once, no per-row kind word):

1. **Explorations**: the open explorations the Explorations list shows (design system repo + each product repo, archived ones left out, as the list leaves them out). Matches name, product, person. Line: the list's status word (lib/explorations-page `statusOf`/`STATE_LABEL`), who explores it (lib/author `explorationAuthorFor`), product: "In review · Sofia · Account". Opens the exploration page.
2. **Library review**: waiting pieces. A reviewer gets every waiting piece, opened in One by one (`?piece=`); anyone else only the pieces they asked for, opened on their list (Library review only links pieces for reviewers). Line: kind + the list's State words ("New size · Waiting 2 days", "2 ways", decided tag, exception).
3. **Being built**: build requests not shipped yet (the page's default filter), its tag + row line, opens the detail (`?request=N`).
4. **Products**: the team's products (library left out), open the product page.
5. **Components** and **Tokens**: as before.
6. **Pages**: Studio's rail pages plus Settings bands (Members, Roles and approvals, Figma and Claude), with former-name keys (history, governance, contrast...). A test keeps them in step with `studioNav()`.

**What loads when**: on first open of the palette, what the page holds lists at once (team model: components, tokens; settings: products; pages). Explorations, pieces and requests come from the same cached reads Studio's pages make (`ghGet` open pulls + `productPulls` + design tasks; `loadLibraryReview` with a new `pictures: false` option so no before/after reads; `loadBuildData`), while the Combobox loading row says "Reading explorations, reviews and build requests". Each read failing adds nothing. No new permission, no token handling, nothing in localStorage. Works on the sample team through `ghGet`'s sample path.

Placeholder and header button: "Search explorations, components, tokens" (Layout.astro `searchLabel`, SearchPalette `placeholderFor`).

Files: `lib/studio-search.ts` (pure builders), `scripts/studio-search.ts` (reads), `lib/palette-search.ts` (`rankGrouped`), `lib/search.ts` (`SearchKind`), `components/ds/SearchPalette.tsx`.

Agent-authored (Claude). No CSS touched. No visual check run here (no headless Chrome on this machine): the visual gate runs later.

### Follow-up (coordinator decisions)

- **One source per fact**: an exploration's status word is the list's own (`explorationState` then `statusOf`, same approvers, same `waitsForLibrary`), with its developers' task and the reviews the list reads (`designTaskStages`, `readReviews`, same cached reads), loaded after the first results paint. Until an input it needs is in, the row shows no status word rather than a different one.
- **First names**: person resolved with the list's rule (`requesterPerson` / Claude AI for agent work / `authorPerson`, `person()` first name): "In review · Sofia · Account".
- **Settings bands per Studio**: Members (`#team` on both), Review rules (`#roles` on both), Figma and Claude (`#figma` on a team's, `#tools` on Bridge's own). A test reads both Settings pages so every anchor exists.

## Risk tier

- [x] Tier 1, low: no component, prop or token change; docs-site behaviour only

## Authored by

- [x] AI agent (Claude), reviewed by a human before merge

## Tests

- `lib/studio-search.test.ts` (new, 11): exploration filter/words/hrefs, piece visibility by role and state words, requests, products, pages vs rail, grouped ranking.
- `components/ds/SearchPalette.studio.test.ts` (new): local results first, loading row, grouped explorations-first, axe clean.
- `SearchPalette.test.ts`: placeholder case added; Library/Bridge behaviour unchanged.
- `npx tsc -p apps/docs-site --noEmit`: no error in touched files (one pre-existing error in ListFilters.tsx from the local workspace link).

body.title: Library: name a team only by a name it has, never its repository in words
body.body:
## What

A team's Library named the team with its repository name turned into words until the team's settings arrived, sometimes for good:

- Hero: "The Bridge demo ds design system", "The Primitives design system"
- Tab title: "Library | Bridge demo ds"

Prod does this too. Gate round 9 saw it in 6 of 6 runs, between 300 ms and 2 s.

## Where it came from

Every Library place that names the team went through `teamDisplayName` (lib/demo.ts). When nothing else is known, its last step turns the repository name into words. The places:

- the tab title and `[data-team-display]` (`scripts/library-team.ts` `paintTeamName`, painted first with no settings);
- the hero and the sentences of the views (`library-data.ts` `systemName`);
- the Library gate's eyebrow;
- the Components lead.

## The rule now

A Library names a team only by a name it has (`lib/recent-teams.ts` `libraryTeamName`):

1. the sample team's fixed name, "Acme Design";
2. the `name` in the team's settings;
3. a name this browser or the account keeps;
4. "Bridge DS" for Bridge's own design system.

Otherwise the name is unknown, and nothing is built from the repository name:

- Tab title: stays "Library | Bridge" as built.
- Hero while the Library reads: a skeleton line, with "Design system" for screen readers.
- Hero once read, for a team whose settings have no name: "Design system".
- Sentences: "this design system".
- Gate eyebrow: "Design system library".

Studio and the other places that use `teamDisplayName` are unchanged.

## Checked

- Headless Chrome against one build, served with the Library rewrite, hero and title logged every 25 ms. That build had this same change on top of #1150:
  - `/library/acme-design-demo/bridge-demo-ds/`: "Library | Acme Design" at 121 ms, then "The Acme Design design system" at 175 ms. The repository name never shows.
  - `?as=sofia`: the same, at 62 and 126 ms.
  - `/library/primer/primitives/`: "Library | Bridge" with the hero "Design system". "Primitives" never shows.
- Tests:
  - `library-team.test.ts`: the title keeps "Library | Bridge" until a name is known; the sample team's title is "Acme Design" at once, even with "Bridge demo ds" kept in this browser.
  - `recent-teams.test.ts`: `libraryTeamName` for each source.
  - `LibraryHome.test.ts`: the hero for an unknown team.
  - The library views, gate and Library suites pass.
- docs-site `tsc`, `lint:css` and `audit:docs` pass.

Up to date with main, #1150 included (merged in, no rebase). The Library files are now exactly what the headless check ran on: #1150 plus this change.

## Review

- [ ] Screens reviewed desktop and mobile (reviewer)
