body.title: One filter pattern: Select inline label + multiple on every Studio filter bar
body.body:
## What changed and why

Owner decision 2026-11-12: Studio uses one filter pattern everywhere. Before this, Library review showed "Status Waiting ▾" (label and value, hugging its content), while Explorations and Being built showed "Not shipped yet ▾" (value only, equal fixed widths, a darker border and a different height). Now every filter is the DS Select with an inline label, and every filter takes several values.

**DS Select (Tier 2, additive props, `minor`)**
- `inlineLabel`: the filter's name inside the trigger in secondary text (`--color-text-muted`), then the value in default text, then the chevron.
  - The trigger hugs its content (min `--size-20`). It keeps Select's border token (`--input-border`), hover and focus.
  - Without a Field label, the label and the value name the trigger together through `aria-labelledby` ("Product: All products"). A combobox doesn't take its name from its content, so this has to be wired explicitly.
- `multiple` + `values` + `onValuesChange`: Base UI's built-in multiple Select. The listbox is `aria-multiselectable`, the list stays open while options are ticked, and Escape closes it and returns focus. These are separate props, so the existing `value` / `onValueChange` types don't change.
- `displayValue`: what the trigger reads instead of the picked label.
- In a hugging trigger, the badge value drops its size container. Otherwise the value would collapse to zero width.
- Added: docs, a `FilterBar` story, an `AllStates` specimen and 4 tests (inline label name and class contract, plain trigger unchanged, keyboard multi-select with axe, `displayValue`). `component-specs.json` regenerated.

**Studio: one filter rule** (`ListFilters` `MultiFilter`, rules in `lib/filter-summary.ts` with tests)
- People, product, family and status filters all take several values, because they combine. Applies to:
  - Library review: Status, Asked by, Product.
  - Explorations and Being built: Status, Product, Person ("People" is now "Person").
  - Every Family filter: Studio Components (`BridgedSelect filter`, `?family=a,b`), Storybook components, team components, and the library's component filter.
  - The Storybook story picker stays a single Select: it is a pick, not a filter.
- Nothing ticked reads as the filter's "all" word ("Not shipped yet", "In progress", "Everyone", "All products", "All"). That word is never an option among its own members, so the aggregate options are removed.
- Each option shows the count tag (`CountTag`, Badge count appearance). This replaces the "(14)" labels and the neutral badges. Library review options now have counts too.
- An option with nothing in it is not listed, unless it is already ticked; then it is listed last so it can be unticked.
- The trigger reads the first ticked option that has items, then "+N" ("Status Being built +1"), never "2 statuses". The old `statusTriggerLabel`, `buildStatusTriggerLabel` and `multiTriggerLabel` helpers are gone.
- Phone (≤ 760px): the filters are one row at one height that scrolls sideways. This applies to Explorations, Being built and Library review.
- Removed: the hand-made `.bl-multi` trigger and its CSS, the Library review Button + Menu trigger and `.lr-filter` CSS, the equal fixed widths, and the unused single-select `ListFiltersBar`.
- Studio Tokens has no Select filter in its bar (only search and an Options panel), so it is unchanged.

**Height: md.** The List/Grid/Board switch is set to `size="sm"`, but its segments are at least the sm control height plus the track inset and border, so it renders at about 38px, close to md. The search fields beside the Family filters are md too, and the Select docs already say md for filter bars. An sm filter (32px) would sit visibly shorter than both.

Agent-authored (Claude Code). Nobody has looked at it in a browser yet: no dev server, Playwright or Storybook build is allowed on this Mac (8 GB). Please check the Vercel preview (Library review, Explorations, Being built, Components, desktop and phone) before merging.

## Risk tier

- [ ] Tier 1, low: docs, stories, lint or a11y fixes, no visual or API change
- [x] Tier 2, medium: new component, variant or prop (additive). Opened as draft until design review
- [ ] Tier 3, high: token added/changed/removed, breaking API, or guardrail change. Design + tech owner approval required

## Authored by

- [ ] Human
- [x] AI agent (Claude), reviewed by a human before merge

## Design review checklist

- [x] Uses tokens only: no hex, rgb, hsl or raw shadows in component CSS (`npm run lint:css` passes)
- [x] Semantic tokens used in components, not primitives, for color and elevation
- [ ] Checked in Storybook in **light and dark** themes (not built locally, see above)
- [ ] Accessibility panel in Storybook shows no violations; keyboard focus is visible (axe passes in vitest on Select, Being built, Explorations, Library review)
- [x] Stories added or updated for every new state
- [x] Changeset added with the right bump (`patch` / `minor` / `major`)
- [x] No lint rule disabled, no test or story deleted (the removed tests covered the removed "2 statuses" helpers; `filter-summary.test.ts` replaces them)
- [ ] Screens comment reviewed: every changed screen looked at, desktop and mobile, light and dark, no render error (docs/VISUAL-CHECK.md)

## Checks run locally

- `vitest` on `apps/docs-site/src/{components,lib,scripts}` plus Select: 410 files, 4964 tests pass. This includes `api-esm-imports.test.ts`.
- `npm run typecheck -w @bridge-ds/react` and `-w @bridge-ds/docs-site`: clean.
- `npm run specs -- --check`: up to date.
- `npm run lint:css`: clean.
- `npm run audit:docs`: 0 imitations, no regression.

Rebase note: #1137 (popup inset 8px) also touches `Select.module.css`, in the popup padding. This PR only adds trigger rules, so a rebase after it merges should be clean.

## Gate review fixes

1. Phone overflow: at 390px the filter row widened the document (Being built 482px, Explorations 453, Library review 425 to 400), so the page scrolled sideways. One `FilterRow` (ListFilters.tsx) now holds the filters of every bar (Explorations, Being built, Library review). On a phone it scrolls inside itself: `overflow-x: auto`, `min-inline-size: 0`, `contain: inline-size` so its content never widens an ancestor; `.bl-bar`, `.bl-narrow` and `.lr-bar-row` take `min-inline-size: 0`, and `.lr` is one `minmax(0, 1fr)` column like `.bl` and `.bb`. Test: ListFilters.test.ts reads the stylesheets and checks those rules.
2. Scroll cue: the edge that hides a filter fades (`mask-image`, fade width `--space-8`), driven by `data-overflow` (start, end, both) that FilterRow sets on scroll, resize and every render. Each filter keeps its full width in the row (`max-inline-size: none`, `flex: none`), so a trigger is never cut mid-word inside the row; only the fade crosses it at the edge. Focus rings get `padding-block` room inside the scroll box. Test: data-overflow per edge with faked scroll sizes.

3. Merged origin/main after Batch B (#1147): the Board follows `filters.status` (Batch B) and `inProgressDefault` stays defined for the Status filter's empty pick, so Explorations renders (new render test, which fails with `ReferenceError: inProgressDefault is not defined` if the definition is dropped). Being built drops `multiTriggerLabel` and its test reads the combobox listbox. Library review keeps FilterRow with Batch B's Info banner (unused `MenuCheckboxItem`/`ChevronDown` imports dropped). `component-specs.json` regenerated.

4. Page still wider than 390px (gate round 10): the visually hidden ": " in each inline-label trigger is `position: absolute`, and neither the trigger nor the row was positioned, so it escaped the scroller and widened the page once the third filter rendered past the edge. Select `.trigger` is now `position: relative`, and so is the phone row. Local build at 390x844, light and dark, sampled every frame for 9 s from navigation: `scrollWidth` 390 throughout on Explorations, Being built and Library review (before: Being built 482, Library review 400). Prod measured 390 on the same pages, so this was introduced by this PR.
5. Focus: inline-label triggers use the DS focus ring (`--focus-ring-width` solid `--focus-ring-color`, `--focus-ring-offset`) instead of the inset field line. The phone row has `--space-1` padding on every side (ring width + offset), offset by negative margins, so the ring is never clipped.

6. Keyboard reach (gate round 11): Tab onto a filter under the fade now scrolls the row (only the row, never the page) so the filter sits fully inside it, the fade width (`scroll-padding-inline: var(--_fade)`) clear on each side (`revealInRow` on focusin in FilterRow).

## UI quality bar

- Gestalt similarity: every filter of every bar is the same control with the same anatomy (name, value, chevron) and the same behaviour (several values, count tags).
- Fitts: md control height (36px comfortable), aligned with the search field and the view switch. No target under 24px, and no hand-made trigger left.
- Progressive disclosure: the bar reads as a sentence ("Status In progress · Product All products · Person Everyone"), with options on demand.

## Screenshots

To be checked on the Vercel preview (no browser on this machine).

No dev server, browser or Storybook build per the CPU rule. No DS package change, so no `npm run specs`.

## Risk tier

- [x] Tier 1, low: docs-site shell only, no DS component, token or API change

## Authored by

- [x] AI agent (Claude), reviewed by a human before merge

## Gate review fixes

Rebased on main (includes #1138, the DS Banner first-line layout). #1147 is still open, so `usePickUp` keeps `rememberBuildWaiting(n)` alone; whoever merges second combines it with `{n, href}`.

1. **Build failed on CSP.** The new pre-paint script's hash (`sha256-Ll3ZCQIvVBR87p07YZjPXIi82senRshd7hNEOX6ljH0=`, recomputed from the final script) is now in `lib/csp.ts` and `vercel.json`. `csp.test.ts` now hashes every static `<script is:inline>` in the source (Layout.astro included) and checks both files, so this mistake fails in unit tests, not only at the end of `astro build`. One `astro build` passes: "every inline script is one of the 11 hashes".
2. **Sofia's Home shift (0.129) and Dana's (0.053).** Root cause: `scripts/demo-gate.ts` unhid the demo strip, then React rendered the banner a frame later. The strip showed empty for a frame (the sample team's reserve only holds while it is hidden), so the whole shell moved up then down (~386 and ~401 ms). Now the banner renders with `flushSync` before the strip unhides, and the strip hides before it empties. The reserve is now the banner's exact height (md button + space-2 block padding + two hairlines: 62px at comfortable density, since control-height-md is 44px; the old reserve was 56px). On the team chip: the sample team's visitor never sees a badge (the account row already says their role), including the badge server-rendered before React runs, so no "Checking"/"Guest" appears and goes away. A pending badge elsewhere has the DS Badge sm box.
3. **Settings shift (0.16).** Same cause as item 2: nothing in #1150 touches a Settings band. The whole page moved when the strip showed empty, and the Library access and Products bands are the large boxes in view. Fixed by item 2.
4. **"Reconnect GitHub" for Dana on the sample team** is hidden: `GitHubAccountMenu` drops it when `data-sample-team` is set (before first paint).
5. **Team menu column (x45 vs x41).** A team row's leading slot grew to its 20px avatar (`width: auto`) while icon rows kept 16px. Every item of the team menu now has one leading slot of `size-5` (the Avatar xs width), with icons centred in it, and the demo mark is sized to match. DS Menu/MenuItem only, contract test added.

Checks: targeted vitest (csp, shell-reserve, TeamChip, GitHubAccountMenu, demo-gate, ProductsNav, load-progress, demo, access-view: 122 passed), docs-site `tsc`, `npm run lint:css`, `npm run audit:docs` (0 imitations, 0 regressed), one `astro build`.

Still needs a visual check (no browser here): CLS on the sample team's Home (Sofia, Dana) and Settings, desktop and phone, with the banner arriving; the team menu's text column measured at 2x.


### Gate round 6 (replaces round 5's Settings gate and floating card)

1. **Team Settings:** I removed the settle gate entirely (`settings-settle.ts`, the hidden groups, the noscript style). Sections render as soon as they are ready. General and Members are now drawn at build time in their final shape (`SettingsSkeletons.tsx`, used as the islands' `slot="fallback"`):

   - Members: the title, a skeleton intro, the table header, then one skeleton row per person in the real row's boxes. That is 5 rows on the sample team. On a next visit it uses the count this browser saw last; otherwise 3.
   - Members' own loading state is the same skeleton.
   - Bands lower down (Products, Library access) have no reserve. They should now start further down the page.

body.title: Token explorer: ramp tiles, family in sync, previews in a fixed box, frame hugs short lists
body.body:
## What changed and why

The owner reported the token explorer and cell editor got worse after #1123. Agent-authored (Claude) fix, compared with the pre-#1123 behaviour.

**Cell editor popover** (`RampPicker.tsx`, `FamilyTabs.tsx`, `inline-edit.ts`)
- Color ramp is a DS RadioGroup of tiles (`appearance="tile"`, #1125): one 32px swatch per step with its step number under it (12px caption), the picked step in the DS checked ring, the value the token had when the editor opened marked "was" (a dot on its swatch, ", was" in its accessible name, and the same dot leads "was neutral.0" in the pick row). No grey track. Arrow keys pick, focus stays on the picked step through the editor's redraws.
- Family tab matches the current value: the editor opens on the value's family (also behind More), a picked step moves the tab to its family, and the DS Tabs are keyed on the family and redrawn once the editor has its final width so the underline sits under the right tab.
- Spacing: one inner padding `--xe-pad` (the footer's, space 4) for title, pick row, tabs, ramp, contrast note, preview and More options; a DS gap (space 2) between the tabs track and More; the title's mode uses the shared `lib/sep` separator.
- The popover width is measured from the tiles (it no longer depends on the SegmentedControl track).

**Grid rows** (`cells.ts`, `token-explorer.css`)
- Root cause: the previews used the class `.xp-stage`, which `exploration-page.css` also styles (padded flex column on a grey plate, loaded on Studio pages through AiToolPanel). With both stylesheets on the page the preview filled the row, spilled out of the edit pill and hid the easing curve. Renamed `.xp-thumb`.
- One fixed border-box box, `flex: none`, clipped, 24px (`--size-6`) in Studio, the color swatch included, centred in the 32px pill of the 40px row.
- Easing: the bezier curve scales to the box. Durations: a bar to scale (capped at 500ms). Shadows: a card of the column's own surface on the column's canvas, so a dark-theme shadow shows on a dark card.
- Every Studio cell keeps the preview slot (empty for types without a picture) and the chevron keeps its room at rest (visibility, not display), so values ("2px", "2 layers") stay on one column at rest and on hover.

**Frame height**
- `.xp` uses `max-height` (viewport) instead of a fixed height with a `size-140` floor, plus a `minmax(0, 1fr)` row: short filtered lists (Shadow 3, Number, Dimension) give a short card; long lists still scroll inside, the detail panel and editor are unchanged. Phones reset to `max-height: none` as before.

**Gate review fixes (second commit, rebased on main)**
- Long values: in the Studio value pill both texts shrink with an ellipsis (`min-width: 0`, `overflow: hidden`) and the pill clips its content, so `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` next to its alias no longer spills 9px past the field; the whole text is on the field's `title` (and in the cell's accessible name, as before).
- Shadow preview: the column's surface card now sits on the column's `color.bg.subtle`, at 60% of the 24px slot, so a light shadow reads in the light column (no more white on white).
- Token details (the phone sheet included): the description wraps, three lines beside the table and whole on a phone, instead of one line cut mid-word.
**Gate round 3 (third commit)**
- Easing rows: the token name (alias) never shrinks (`flex: none`); only the resolved value ellipsizes. Easings show their curve and the four numbers (`0.16, 1, 0.3, 1`) instead of `easing.…` next to `cubic-bezier(…`; the title keeps `cubic-bezier(...)` whole and the accessible name starts with the visible text.
- Type filter: the segments wrap onto a second line instead of scrolling behind the edge fade, so "All 119" never reads as a bare "119".

**Targeted gate fixes (fourth commit)**
- Easing cells stack: the token name on the first line, the four numbers on their own line under it (they wrap at a comma in a narrow column, never an ellipsis), kept when the details panel is open; one space between them in the text.
- Type filter on desktop: one row at the control height; the types never shrink and the search field gives way first (min size 40). The types wrap only on a phone. With the details panel open on a laptop they may still scroll with the DS edge fade rather than push the toolbar past the table.
- Round 5 (fifth commit): no spacer between the types and Options on a desktop; the search takes all the free width (`flex: 1 1 auto`, min size 40), the types keep their natural width, Options ends the row. Editor step list values (16px, `cubic-bezier(...)`) use the mono face of the pick row.
- Easing (and size, duration) editor: the original step carries the "was" dot and word like the pick row, no more ", was" glued to the value; the edge of the step list that hides more steps fades and the picked step scrolls into view inside the list (never the page); the pick row shows the resolved value for every type.
- Family tabs (sixth commit, after #1149 merged): the underline DS Tabs, per the tab-like controls rule (Tabs switch sections), no more deprecated `contained` look; the test asserts the underline variant.
- Round 6 (seventh commit): from 861px the toolbar is one row that never exceeds its container: the search grows into the free width but never shrinks under size 40 (`flex: 1 0 var(--size-40)`), the types keep their natural width when it fits and otherwise shrink with their DS track scrolling under the edge fade, Options (`flex: none`) always stays in view. Hex values are never cut: the hex never shrinks and the mode column keeps room for preview, palette name, full `#rrggbb` and chevron (17rem in edit, 16rem in read-only Studio rows; a narrower table scrolls sideways). The underline tabs' grey baseline runs on under "More" in the editor.
- Round 7 (eighth commit): the search's basis and minimum are the box (size 40 + size 12, 208px), so its text area keeps about 150px and "Filter 119 tokens" reads whole (at size 40 the 160px box left a 102px text area); the types give way first. The editor's grey baseline is drawn on the family row itself, across its width, so it runs under "More" (tabs and More sit on its bottom edge). Studio names stay on one line: the name column keeps 15rem, a longer name ends in an ellipsis with the full path on hover, names wrap at their dots only on a phone; the details panel no longer hides the hex, and the table, as wide as its column minimums, scrolls sideways instead of squeezing names and values.
- Round 8 (ninth commit): a Studio name stays on one line with an ellipsis in every row state (selected, hovered, row menu shown) on a desktop. The desktop rendering has no break points at all (a `<wbr>` can still break a nowrap line in some browsers); a second copy with a break point after each dot shows only on a phone (the other is `display: none`, so it is read once). Every name cell carries the full path as its title. The row menu keeps its room (opacity), so the name never narrows when it shows.

## Risk tier

- [x] Tier 1, low: docs-site only, no DS component, token or API change

## Authored by

- [x] AI agent (Claude), reviewed by a human before merge

## Checks run

- Targeted vitest: `scripts/explorer` (family-tabs, xss, xss-studio, new explorer-layout), `components/explorer`, `lib/explorer`, `lib/html-sinks`, `lib/api-esm-imports`: 102 tests pass (tab-like-controls included) after the gate fixes (ellipsis, shadow backdrop, description wrap, alias-whole, easing stack, toolbar min widths, hex room, name column (every row state, title on every name), step list and tabs baseline contracts added).
- New tests: ramp tiles (step numbers, swatches, checked, was marker, arrow keys, focus kept, axe), family tab sync (opens on the value's family behind More, follows a picked step), preview sizing contract (fixed box, one slot per Studio cell, curve, duration bar, shadow card, chevron room), frame max-height contract, editor padding and More gap contract.
- `npm run lint:css` clean. `npm run audit:docs`: imitations 0 (0 since baseline), hardcoded unchanged. docs-site typecheck shows no errors in changed files.
- No dev server, browser or Storybook build was run (CPU rule): **visuals need the separate reviewer's look** (editor popover light/dark, Studio rows at rest and hover, Shadow/Number filtered frames, Library /tokens/).

## Design review checklist

- [x] Uses tokens only (`npm run lint:css` passes)
- [x] Semantic tokens for color and elevation
- [ ] Checked in light and dark (pending reviewer screenshots)
- [x] Changeset added (`@bridge-ds/docs-site` patch)
- [x] No lint rule disabled, no test or story deleted (the SegmentedControl ramp test was rewritten for the tiles)

body.title: fix(core): library re-ask lost when its changes answer shares the millisecond
body.body:
Fixes the intermittent CI failure in `packages/core/test/two-reviews-github.test.ts` > "library Ask for changes: back to Exploring, the design yes stays and is not asked again" (`expected false to be true` on `isInReview` after `answerLeadOnGitHub`).

## Cause

A real logic bug, not only a test timing issue. `libraryPendingOf` (`packages/core/src/explorations.ts`) asks a piece again when its answer is "changes" given **before** the new ask:

```ts
return !d || (d.verdict === 'changes' && d.at < asked);
```

When the designer's answer (`answerLeadOnGitHub`, which writes `library.askedAt`) lands in the same millisecond as the library's Ask for changes (`decidePieceOnGitHub`, which writes the decision's `at`), `d.at === asked`, so the piece is not pending, `isInReview` is false, and the exploration sits with nothing waiting on anyone. Under CI load the test steps run within one millisecond; fast automation (an agent answering right away) can hit it for real.

## Fix

Compare with `<=`. Safe because a "changes" answer always takes the ask away (`withoutReviewAsks`), so a standing ask with the same timestamp was necessarily written after it.

## Test

New case "library Ask for changes answered in the same millisecond" runs the whole flow with one frozen `date`: it failed before the fix with the exact CI error and passes now. Core `two-reviews-github`, `two-reviews`, `exploration-lead` tests pass; `tsc` on core is clean. Changeset: `@bridge-ds/core` patch.

body.title: Tab-like controls: one logic, one selected look each, focus ring keyboard only
body.body:
## What changed and why

The owner wants one logic for tab-like controls, written once and applied everywhere. Today the Settings tabs could show a heavy blue rounded box on the selected tab, the token type filter marked its selected segment with a Deep Harbor outline that reads as keyboard focus, and count tags changed look when selected. Agent-authored (Claude), session linked below.

### The rule (Tabs.docs.json, SegmentedControl.docs.json, docs/DESIGN-LANGUAGE.md section 7, AGENTS.md "UI quality bar")

- **Tabs (underline)** switch the SECTIONS or PANELS of one page or object: Settings (Team, Reviews, Tools, You), a component page (Usage, Tokens, Code, Changelog), the color families in the token editor.
- **SegmentedControl** switches a VIEW or a FILTER of the same content: List, Grid or Board; the token type filter; Light or Dark; compare Side by side or Overlay; the expression picker.
- Never a third look, never custom tab-like CSS.
- **Tabs selected** = ink text + the signal underline. Unselected = muted text. No box, no outline, no fill on the selection.
- **SegmentedControl selected** = raised plate on the subtle track (`surface.raised`, `border.emphasis` hairline, `elevation.raised`), ink text. Never a Deep Harbor or focus-colored outline.
- **Focus ring**: `:focus-visible` only (keyboard), inside the tab or segment a step off its edge (`focus-ring-width + focus-ring-offset`). A pointer focus draws nothing, the browser's ring included.
- **Counts** use the component's count slot and look the same selected or not.
- **Link mode** (segments with `href`) wears the same plate on the current page. `appearance="strong"` (the Deep Harbor fill) is explicit and used only by the global Library/Studio space switch.
- Tabs `variant="contained"` is deprecated (JSDoc + docs). It now wears the SegmentedControl plate, so there are still only two looks.

### Code

- `Tabs.module.css`: `.tab:focus:not(:focus-visible) { outline: none }`, an inset ring with offset, the selected count override removed, contained plate aligned with SegmentedControl.
- `SegmentedControl.module.css`: selected border `control-checked-bg` → `border-emphasis`. Link-mode `aria-current` no longer falls into the strong fill without `.strong`. Selected count overrides removed. Pointer-focus outline dropped. Inset ring with offset.
- Call sites: `SpaceSwitch.tsx` now passes `appearance="strong"`, so the space switch keeps its solid Deep Harbor current segment. `FaceSetting.tsx` face parts (Hair / Glasses / Beard / Expression panels) go from contained to underline Tabs, which also removes a contained-tabs-over-segmented stack. No site CSS restyled a selection (grep, and now a test enforces it).
- Not touched: `FamilyTabs.tsx` (token editor families still `variant="contained"`), which belongs to agent/token-explorer-fixes. By this rule it should drop `variant="contained"`.

### Tests

- New `apps/docs-site/src/lib/tab-like-controls.test.ts` checks CSS contracts on the DS sources. The react test project empties stylesheets and jsdom has no `:focus-visible`, so these run in the node docs project. Checks: the selected state uses the indicator or plate tokens and never focus-ring, outline or Deep Harbor (except under `.strong`); focus-ring tokens appear only under `:focus-visible`; no count rule is keyed by selection; no site stylesheet paints a selected segment or tab.
- React tests: link mode adds the strong class only with `appearance="strong"`; a clicked tab is selected, with axe.
- Ran: targeted vitest for Tabs, SegmentedControl, dom/segmented-control, FaceSetting, space-switch and the new contract test (all pass). Typecheck passes for react and docs-site. `npm run lint:css` passes. `npm run specs` regenerated. `npm run audit:docs` passes: 0 imitations, 100% adoption, no regression. body.title: Popup lists get an 8px inset; See it as matches Get started
body.body:
## What changed and why

Owner decision: the DS popup inset was too tight at 4px. Agent-authored (Claude Code).

- **DS (`@bridge-ds/react`, minor, visual change):** Menu, Select and Combobox popups pad with `var(--space-2)` (8px) instead of `var(--space-1)`. Item radius stays concentric: `calc(var(--popup-radius) - var(--space-2))`, which gives 20 - 8 = **12px on Bridge** (the existing `radius.control` / `radius.xl` step) and 16 - 8 = **8px on Ocean** (no primitive step at 8, but the calc keeps it exact, so no token is needed). Separators use `margin: var(--space-2) calc(var(--space-2) * -1)`: the inset's gap above and below, still running to the popup edge. No other DS component uses the popup item list inset (Popover is a content surface with `space-4`, SidebarNav is not a popup).
- **Combobox inline mode:** it has no popup surface, so no inset is added there: the always-open list keeps its edges aligned with the field above (the field-to-list gap is already `space-2`), and its items keep `radius-control`, which now equals the popup items' radius on Bridge. Note: Combobox's `.separator` class is not rendered by Combobox.tsx (only Select renders one); it was updated anyway for consistency.
- **Specs + docs:** `npm run specs` regenerated `component-specs.json` (popup padding `space.2`, item `cornerRadius: calc(popup.radius - space.2)`). Anatomy in Menu/Select/Combobox `docs.json` states the inset, concentric corners and separator gap. No Figma plugin fixture asserted the old padding.
- **Docs site compensations removed:** the account menu head (`.acc-menu-head`) and the See it as footer note (`.see-as-note`) carried their own `space-3` side padding; the menu inset now does the outer spacing: the account head uses `space-1 space-2` (lines up with the item icons), and the See it as note starts on the items' text column after the radio slot and the face (`calc(space-2 + icon-size-sm + space-2 + size-6 + space-3)`). The note's hand-drawn top border is replaced by a DS `MenuSeparator`. Team menu, row menu, family tabs, list filter and search palette had no inset compensation to remove.

body.title: Sample team: Add a product for Dana, run in this browser
body.body:
## What changed and why

Owner question (2026-11-13): "why, when I click Start an exploration, is the path to add a new product no longer available?" On the sample team (acme-design-demo/bridge-demo-ds) "Add a product" only showed for a GitHub admin or lead (`useCanAddProduct` / `canAddProduct`), and the sample visitor never is one, even when they "See it as" Dana. Agent-authored (Claude Code).

**Who sees it.** On the sample team, the person played in "See it as" when they run the team: Dana (admin and lead), via the new pure rule `canAddSampleProduct` (lib/add-product.ts) on the played member (`currentContributor`, lib/demo-cast `playedMember`). Sofia and Leo (designers), Ann (product manager) and Malik (developer, no email membership) never see it, as on a real team. Real teams keep the exact old rule.

**Where.** Everywhere AddProduct shows for an admin: Start an exploration's Where list (last option after the separator), Settings > Products on the team shell (TeamProducts), All products. Same dialog, validated board "Add a product v3", not redesigned.

**What runs in this browser.** "add a product" joins `SAMPLE_IN_BROWSER` (lib/demo.ts) with a dialog line in `ACTION_LINES`. Submitting keeps the entry with `keepSampleProduct` (lib/demo-in-browser.ts) under `bridge.acme-design-demo/bridge-demo-ds.draft.products` in localStorage: same storage, same lifetime and same reset as the in-browser starts (`swapDemoDrafts` drops it when the visitor leaves the sample team). `addedHere` (scripts/repo-context.ts) merges it into the team's settings on the sample team only, so the side nav "Products", the product page and the Where list read it. Nothing is sent: no `addToTeam`, no GitHub reads, no POST (tests stub fetch and assert no write call).

**Sample-friendly steps (what I decided).**
- "Its code is on GitHub": no account is read on the sample team, and the card is not marked Recommended there ("Only its address" is). The step shows one drawing and one line, `sampleFoundLine` in lib/add-product.ts, built from the card labels ("On the sample team, Bridge does not look for code on an account. Try Only its address or It's a new product."), with Back only. No Find it on GitHub, no owners' request.
- A product added in this browser shows no "One step before the first preview" setup step on its page (nothing exists to connect).
- "Only its address" and "It's a new product": same form, no code started on GitHub, no linking, no pending-action. The entry keeps only key, name and address (no repo, no designers' copy, no previews).
- "Give designers their own copy" is hidden on the sample team: nothing would be copied. No copy-access or previews step.
- The form's status line says it once, before submitting: `DEMO_WORDS.sampleProduct`, "On the sample team it stays in this browser."
- After adding from Settings, its page opens (as before). After adding from Start an exploration, on every team (real teams too, as StartExploration's header promises), the person comes back to Start with the new product picked: AddProduct's new `onAdded(key)` replaces opening the page there, and the product is known at once (`noteAddedProduct` / `addedHere`). "Sent for review" still shows only for a reviewed add.

**Fix, also on main (real teams): the dialog never finished closing.** Closing Add a product from a form step (It's a new product, Only its address), by Escape or after adding from Start, reset the step to the first question during Base UI's exit. The form step is its own component (StartNewProduct), so the popup remounted mid-exit, the exit never completed, and its see-through backdrop (pointer-events auto) stayed over the page: nothing was clickable. Same code on main, so real teams had it from Settings too. Now the step (and the review step) stays as it is while closing, and each new opening starts from the question (reset before paint). Back from a step also puts the focus on its card again (Base UI's trap had moved it to the popup). Test: "Add a product closes cleanly from every step" (fails on the old code, popup and backdrop still mounted).

**Tests.** demo.test.ts (action line), demo-in-browser.test.ts (runsInBrowser, keep/replace/drop on leaving, broken copies, voice), add-product.test.ts (canAddSampleProduct over the whole cast), AddProduct.test.ts (Dana sees it; GitHub card reads nothing; address path adds in browser, opens its page, no addToTeam, no write; from Start hands back the key; Sofia sees nothing), StartExploration.test.ts (Dana adds "Atlas" from Where: comes back picked, no write, shows in ProductsNav; Sofia, Leo, Ann and Malik don't see it; real-team email admin still doesn't; real team with the add API stubbed: added from Where, back to Start with it picked, its page not opened). `npx tsc -p apps/docs-site --noEmit` is clean on touched files (one pre-existing ListFilters error). body.title: Library: name a team only by a name it has, never its repository in words
body.body:
## What

A team's Library named the team with its repository name turned into words until the team's settings arrived, sometimes for good:

- Hero: "The Bridge demo ds design system", "The Primitives design system"
- Tab title: "Library | Bridge demo ds"

Prod does this too. Gate round 9 saw it in 6 of 6 runs, between 300 ms and 2 s.

## Where it came from

Every Library place that names the team went through `teamDisplayName` (lib/demo.ts). When nothing else is known, its last step turns the repository name into words. The places:

- the tab title and `[data-team-display]` (`scripts/library-team.ts` `paintTeamName`, painted first with no settings);
- the hero and the sentences of the views (`library-data.ts` `systemName`);
- the Library gate's eyebrow;
- the Components lead.

## The rule now

A Library names a team only by a name it has (`lib/recent-teams.ts` `libraryTeamName`):

1. the sample team's fixed name, "Acme Design";
2. the `name` in the team's settings;
3. a name this browser or the account keeps;
4. "Bridge DS" for Bridge's own design system.

Otherwise the name is unknown, and nothing is built from the repository name:

- Tab title: stays "Library | Bridge" as built.
- Hero while the Library reads: a skeleton line, with "Design system" for screen readers.
- Hero once read, for a team whose settings have no name: "Design system".
- Sentences: "this design system".
- Gate eyebrow: "Design system library".

Studio and the other places that use `teamDisplayName` are unchanged.

## Checked

- Headless Chrome against one build, served with the Library rewrite, hero and title logged every 25 ms. That build had this same change on top of #1150:
  - `/library/acme-design-demo/bridge-demo-ds/`: "Library | Acme Design" at 121 ms, then "The Acme Design design system" at 175 ms. The repository name never shows.
  - `?as=sofia`: the same, at 62 and 126 ms.
  - `/library/primer/primitives/`: "Library | Bridge" with the hero "Design system". "Primitives" never shows.
- Tests:
  - `library-team.test.ts`: the title keeps "Library | Bridge" until a name is known; the sample team's title is "Acme Design" at once, even with "Bridge demo ds" kept in this browser.
  - `recent-teams.test.ts`: `libraryTeamName` for each source.

body.title: One filter pattern: Select inline label + multiple on every Studio filter bar
body.body:
## What changed and why

Owner decision 2026-11-12: Studio uses one filter pattern everywhere. Before this, Library review showed "Status Waiting ▾" (label and value, hugging its content), while Explorations and Being built showed "Not shipped yet ▾" (value only, equal fixed widths, a darker border and a different height). Now every filter is the DS Select with an inline label, and every filter takes several values.

**DS Select (Tier 2, additive props, `minor`)**
- `inlineLabel`: the filter's name inside the trigger in secondary text (`--color-text-muted`), then the value in default text, then the chevron.
  - The trigger hugs its content (min `--size-20`). It keeps Select's border token (`--input-border`), hover and focus.
  - Without a Field label, the label and the value name the trigger together through `aria-labelledby` ("Product: All products"). A combobox doesn't take its name from its content, so this has to be wired explicitly.
- `multiple` + `values` + `onValuesChange`: Base UI's built-in multiple Select. The listbox is `aria-multiselectable`, the list stays open while options are ticked, and Escape closes it and returns focus. These are separate props, so the existing `value` / `onValueChange` types don't change.
- `displayValue`: what the trigger reads instead of the picked label.
- In a hugging trigger, the badge value drops its size container. Otherwise the value would collapse to zero width.
- Added: docs, a `FilterBar` story, an `AllStates` specimen and 4 tests (inline label name and class contract, plain trigger unchanged, keyboard multi-select with axe, `displayValue`). `component-specs.json` regenerated.

**Studio: one filter rule** (`ListFilters` `MultiFilter`, rules in `lib/filter-summary.ts` with tests)
- People, product, family and status filters all take several values, because they combine. Applies to:
  - Library review: Status, Asked by, Product.
  - Explorations and Being built: Status, Product, Person ("People" is now "Person").
  - Every Family filter: Studio Components (`BridgedSelect filter`, `?family=a,b`), Storybook components, team components, and the library's component filter.
  - The Storybook story picker stays a single Select: it is a pick, not a filter.
- Nothing ticked reads as the filter's "all" word ("Not shipped yet", "In progress", "Everyone", "All products", "All"). That word is never an option among its own members, so the aggregate options are removed.
- Each option shows the count tag (`CountTag`, Badge count appearance). This replaces the "(14)" labels and the neutral badges. Library review options now have counts too.
- An option with nothing in it is not listed, unless it is already ticked; then it is listed last so it can be unticked.
- The trigger reads the first ticked option that has items, then "+N" ("Status Being built +1"), never "2 statuses". The old `statusTriggerLabel`, `buildStatusTriggerLabel` and `multiTriggerLabel` helpers are gone.
- Phone (≤ 760px): the filters are one row at one height that scrolls sideways. This applies to Explorations, Being built and Library review.
- Removed: the hand-made `.bl-multi` trigger and its CSS, the Library review Button + Menu trigger and `.lr-filter` CSS, the equal fixed widths, and the unused single-select `ListFiltersBar`.
- Studio Tokens has no Select filter in its bar (only search and an Options panel), so it is unchanged.

**Height: md.** The List/Grid/Board switch is set to `size="sm"`, but its segments are at least the sm control height plus the track inset and border, so it renders at about 38px, close to md. The search fields beside the Family filters are md too, and the Select docs already say md for filter bars. An sm filter (32px) would sit visibly shorter than both.

Agent-authored (Claude Code). Nobody has looked at it in a browser yet: no dev server, Playwright or Storybook build is allowed on this Mac (8 GB). Please check the Vercel preview (Library review, Explorations, Being built, Components, desktop and phone) before merging.

- [x] Tier 2, medium: new component, variant or prop (additive). Opened as draft until design review
- [ ] Tier 3, high: token added/changed/removed, breaking API, or guardrail change. Design + tech owner approval required

Test: ListFilters.test.ts reads the stylesheets and checks those rules.
2. Scroll cue: the edge that hides a filter fades (`mask-image`, fade width `--space-8`), driven by `data-overflow` (start, end, both) that FilterRow sets on scroll, resize and every render. Each filter keeps its full width in the row (`max-inline-size: none`, `flex: none`), so a trigger is never cut mid-word inside the row; only the fade crosses it at the edge. Focus rings get `padding-block` room inside the scroll box. Test: data-overflow per edge with faked scroll sizes.

3. Merged origin/main after Batch B (#1147): the Board follows `filters.status` (Batch B) and `inProgressDefault` stays defined for the Status filter's empty pick, so Explorations renders (new render test, which fails with `ReferenceError: inProgressDefault is not defined` if the definition is dropped). Being built drops `multiTriggerLabel` and its test reads the combobox listbox. Library review keeps FilterRow with Batch B's Info banner (unused `MenuCheckboxItem`/`ChevronDown` imports dropped). `component-specs.json` regenerated.

4. Page still wider than 390px (gate round 10): the visually hidden ": " in each inline-label trigger is `position: absolute`, and neither the trigger nor the row was positioned, so it escaped the scroller and widened the page once the third filter rendered past the edge. Select `.trigger` is now `position: relative`, and so is the phone row. Local build at 390x844, light and dark, sampled every frame for 9 s from navigation: `scrollWidth` 390 throughout on Explorations, Being built and Library review (before: Being built 482, Library review 400). Prod measured 390 on the same pages, so this was introduced by this PR.
5. Focus: inline-label triggers use the DS focus ring (`--focus-ring-width` solid `--focus-ring-color`, `--focus-ring-offset`) instead of the inset field line. The phone row has `--space-1` padding on every side (ring width + offset), offset by negative margins, so the ring is never clipped.

6. Keyboard reach (gate round 11): Tab onto a filter under the fade now scrolls the row (only the row, never the page) so the filter sits fully inside it, the fade width (`scroll-padding-inline: var(--_fade)`) clear on each side (`revealInRow` on focusin in FilterRow).

body.title: Token explorer: ramp tiles, family in sync, previews in a fixed box, frame hugs short lists
body.body:
## What changed and why

The owner reported the token explorer and cell editor got worse after #1123. Agent-authored (Claude) fix, compared with the pre-#1123 behaviour.

**Cell editor popover** (`RampPicker.tsx`, `FamilyTabs.tsx`, `inline-edit.ts`)
- Color ramp is a DS RadioGroup of tiles (`appearance="tile"`, #1125): one 32px swatch per step with its step number under it (12px caption), the picked step in the DS checked ring, the value the token had when the editor opened marked "was" (a dot on its swatch, ", was" in its accessible name, and the same dot leads "was neutral.0" in the pick row). No grey track. Arrow keys pick, focus stays on the picked step through the editor's redraws.
- Family tab matches the current value: the editor opens on the value's family (also behind More), a picked step moves the tab to its family, and the DS Tabs are keyed on the family and redrawn once the editor has its final width so the underline sits under the right tab.
- Spacing: one inner padding `--xe-pad` (the footer's, space 4) for title, pick row, tabs, ramp, contrast note, preview and More options; a DS gap (space 2) between the tabs track and More; the title's mode uses the shared `lib/sep` separator.
- The popover width is measured from the tiles (it no longer depends on the SegmentedControl track).

**Grid rows** (`cells.ts`, `token-explorer.css`)
- Root cause: the previews used the class `.xp-stage`, which `exploration-page.css` also styles (padded flex column on a grey plate, loaded on Studio pages through AiToolPanel). With both stylesheets on the page the preview filled the row, spilled out of the edit pill and hid the easing curve. Renamed `.xp-thumb`.
- One fixed border-box box, `flex: none`, clipped, 24px (`--size-6`) in Studio, the color swatch included, centred in the 32px pill of the 40px row.
- Easing: the bezier curve scales to the box. Durations: a bar to scale (capped at 500ms). Shadows: a card of the column's own surface on the column's canvas, so a dark-theme shadow shows on a dark card.
- Every Studio cell keeps the preview slot (empty for types without a picture) and the chevron keeps its room at rest (visibility, not display), so values ("2px", "2 layers") stay on one column at rest and on hover.

**Frame height**
- `.xp` uses `max-height` (viewport) instead of a fixed height with a `size-140` floor, plus a `minmax(0, 1fr)` row: short filtered lists (Shadow 3, Number, Dimension) give a short card; long lists still scroll inside, the detail panel and editor are unchanged. Phones reset to `max-height: none` as before.

**Gate review fixes (second commit, rebased on main)**
- Long values: in the Studio value pill both texts shrink with an ellipsis (`min-width: 0`, `overflow: hidden`) and the pill clips its content, so `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` next to its alias no longer spills 9px past the field; the whole text is on the field's `title` (and in the cell's accessible name, as before).
- Shadow preview: the column's surface card now sits on the column's `color.bg.subtle`, at 60% of the 24px slot, so a light shadow reads in the light column (no more white on white).
- Token details (the phone sheet included): the description wraps, three lines beside the table and whole on a phone, instead of one line cut mid-word.
**Gate round 3 (third commit)**
- Easing rows: the token name (alias) never shrinks (`flex: none`); only the resolved value ellipsizes. Easings show their curve and the four numbers (`0.16, 1, 0.3, 1`) instead of `easing.…` next to `cubic-bezier(…`; the title keeps `cubic-bezier(...)` whole and the accessible name starts with the visible text.
- Type filter: the segments wrap onto a second line instead of scrolling behind the edge fade, so "All 119" never reads as a bare "119".

**Targeted gate fixes (fourth commit)**
- Easing cells stack: the token name on the first line, the four numbers on their own line under it (they wrap at a comma in a narrow column, never an ellipsis), kept when the details panel is open; one space between them in the text.
- Type filter on desktop: one row at the control height; the types never shrink and the search field gives way first (min size 40). The types wrap only on a phone. With the details panel open on a laptop they may still scroll with the DS edge fade rather than push the toolbar past the table.
- Round 5 (fifth commit): no spacer between the types and Options on a desktop; the search takes all the free width (`flex: 1 1 auto`, min size 40), the types keep their natural width, Options ends the row. Editor step list values (16px, `cubic-bezier(...)`) use the mono face of the pick row.
- Easing (and size, duration) editor: the original step carries the "was" dot and word like the pick row, no more ", was" glued to the value; the edge of the step list that hides more steps fades and the picked step scrolls into view inside the list (never the page); the pick row shows the resolved value for every type.
- Family tabs (sixth commit, after #1149 merged): the underline DS Tabs, per the tab-like controls rule (Tabs switch sections), no more deprecated `contained` look; the test asserts the underline variant.
- Round 6 (seventh commit): from 861px the toolbar is one row that never exceeds its container: the search grows into the free width but never shrinks under size 40 (`flex: 1 0 var(--size-40)`), the types keep their natural width when it fits and otherwise shrink with their DS track scrolling under the edge fade, Options (`flex: none`) always stays in view. Hex values are never cut: the hex never shrinks and the mode column keeps room for preview, palette name, full `#rrggbb` and chevron (17rem in edit, 16rem in read-only Studio rows; a narrower table scrolls sideways). The underline tabs' grey baseline runs on under "More" in the editor.
- Round 7 (eighth commit): the search's basis and minimum are the box (size 40 + size 12, 208px), so its text area keeps about 150px and "Filter 119 tokens" reads whole (at size 40 the 160px box left a 102px text area); the types give way first. The editor's grey baseline is drawn on the family row itself, across its width, so it runs under "More" (tabs and More sit on its bottom edge). Studio names stay on one line: the name column keeps 15rem, a longer name ends in an ellipsis with the full path on hover, names wrap at their dots only on a phone; the details panel no longer hides the hex, and the table, as wide as its column minimums, scrolls sideways instead of squeezing names and values.
- Round 8 (ninth commit): a Studio name stays on one line with an ellipsis in every row state (selected, hovered, row menu shown) on a desktop. The desktop rendering has no break points at all (a `<wbr>` can still break a nowrap line in some browsers); a second copy with a break point after each dot shows only on a phone (the other is `display: none`, so it is read once). Every name cell carries the full path as its title. The row menu keeps its room (opacity), so the name never narrows when it shows.

body.title: fix(core): library re-ask lost when its changes answer shares the millisecond
body.body:
Fixes the intermittent CI failure in `packages/core/test/two-reviews-github.test.ts` > "library Ask for changes: back to Exploring, the design yes stays and is not asked again" (`expected false to be true` on `isInReview` after `answerLeadOnGitHub`).

## Cause

A real logic bug, not only a test timing issue. `libraryPendingOf` (`packages/core/src/explorations.ts`) asks a piece again when its answer is "changes" given **before** the new ask:

```ts
return !d || (d.verdict === 'changes' && d.at < asked);
```

When the designer's answer (`answerLeadOnGitHub`, which writes `library.askedAt`) lands in the same millisecond as the library's Ask for changes (`decidePieceOnGitHub`, which writes the decision's `at`), `d.at === asked`, so the piece is not pending, `isInReview` is false, and the exploration sits with nothing waiting on anyone. Under CI load the test steps run within one millisecond; fast automation (an agent answering right away) can hit it for real.

## Fix

Compare with `<=`. Safe because a "changes" answer always takes the ask away (`withoutReviewAsks`), so a standing ask with the same timestamp was necessarily written after it.

## Test

New case "library Ask for changes answered in the same millisecond" runs the whole flow with one frozen `date`: it failed before the fix with the exact CI error and passes now. Core `two-reviews-github`, `two-reviews`, `exploration-lead` tests pass; `tsc` on core is clean. Changeset: `@bridge-ds/core` patch.

## What changed and why

High severity findings of the product review of prod on the sample team (`/studio/acme-design-demo/bridge-demo-ds/`). Agent-authored (Claude Code).

**D1, Settings > Reviews (personal data).** The sample repo's `bridge.config.json` names the account hosting it as design owner, and Studio merged it into the demo: "Dana and peterbono decide what the library keeps". Now the sample team names only its cast: `reviewGithubOwners` (lib/team-reviews.ts) returns none on the sample team and is used by ReviewsSection and team-reviews-data; `withSampleReviews` also drops GitHub owners and non-cast logins. The GitHub owners note no longer says `bridge.config.json (governance.owners.design)`. Settings > Review rules' "For developers" fold labels the rights "Checks the look" / "Checks the code" / "Adds it to the library" (not `governance.rights.*`) and lists owners through `teamEntries` (cast only on the sample team).

**D2 / D3, names and addresses (personal data).** Changed in strings a demo visitor can see:
- Color specimen: "Edited 2 hours ago by Florian" -> "by Dana" (components/foundations/Specimens.tsx)
- Token editor preview Avatar: "Florian Gouloubi" -> "Ana Lima" (components/EditorPreview.tsx)
- Card docs + story: "Design: Florian G." -> "Design: Dana." (Card.docs.json, Card.stories.tsx)
- Avatar docs + stories: "Florian Gouloubi" -> "Ana Lima" / "Sam Rivera", illustrated seed "peterbono" -> "ana-lima"
- Component page Code tab: the raw Storybook address (`https://bridge-storybook.floriangouloubi.com`, from the sample repo's config) is no longer printed; the "open in Storybook" link stays. No public Storybook exists on bridgedesignsystem.com (checked), so the link keeps the configured address.
- core owner-entry error example: "peterbono" -> "octocat"
- Left alone on purpose: About page, Landing/Layout `meta author`, the home "Connect" card (deliberate maker credit), docs/security.astro (states the former domain for installed plugins), code comments, vercel.json, schema descriptions, test fixtures, `TEMPLATE_REPO` (a real repository). The sample repo's own `bridge.config.json` (outside this repo) still names peterbono as owner and the old Storybook address: it is no longer shown, but it could be cleaned there too.

**C6, demo actions.** On the sample team, "Start an exploration" and "Looks right" run in this browser instead of opening the "This is a sample team" gate (`SAMPLE_IN_BROWSER` / `runsInBrowser` in lib/demo.ts, skipped by scripts/demo-gate.ts). Start opens the real dialog; Start keeps the exploration for the visit and says "Started in this browser ... With your own team, Claude AI opens it on a live preview" with "Get started". Looks right moves the exploration on exactly as the real approval (core `designApproveOnGitHub`, two-reviews rules) would (`sampleLooksRight`, lib/demo-in-browser.ts): the design review's yes; then, when no new piece waits on the library, the hand-off `settleReviewsOnGitHub` runs (Done exploring in the description, `exploration` label off, `ready-for-devs` on): Ready to build. While a new piece waits, it stays In review on the library decision (Dana's own when she holds both hats). The answered pull request is kept for the visit and every `ghGet` read of the sample team's pull requests is answered with it (`sampleRead`, scripts/github-session.ts), so the exploration page, the lists, Home and the Explorations rail badge agree. Fix after gate review: the first version only recorded the yes, so a screen with nothing for the library fell back to Exploring. Gate round 3: the sample flows were asked before the two reviews (one ask to the lead, no library ask on record), so core saw no library piece pending and handed Order fulfilment timeline to the developers, which also showed Timeline as added. The library ask is now read as the exploration page reads it (`legacyLibraryAsk`) and written down, so it stays In review on Dana's library decision and no piece is decided by Looks right. Answers are keyed by the pull request's own repository; after one, reads are marked fresh, the Explorations list reads again (`SAMPLE_ANSWERED_EVENT`) and the rail badge recounts (`recountWaitingExplorations`). Deal pipeline cards: its Card restyle is 12px padding, which core reads as Card Compact (`asIsOption`), so no list ever counts a library decision on it and Looks right hands it off as the real approval does; the page's "Add to the library" there is the cross-screen Card padding choice with Order, which the two-reviews rule keeps out of the design review (`looksRightBlock` off with hats). Gate round 5: Home's age tag read "New today" on the library decision left after Looks right, because the waiting clock (`turnSince`, lib/lead-decisions.ts, shared by Home and the Explorations list) restarted at the last decision. A looks-right never starts a wait now: the clock runs from the last other decision, else the library ask, else the design ask, so it reads "Waiting 5 days" (amber once late) on every team, not only the sample. Gate round 6: an Explorations row whose line says a review waits on the viewer (its turn, or a library decision Explorations leaves to Library review) showed its last change ("yesterday"); it now shows Home's tag from the same clock (`rowTime` in lib/lead-decisions.ts: `turnSince` + `waitingLabel`, "Waiting 5 days"). Rows that don't wait on the viewer keep their last-change time. Said once: next to a line that already starts with "Waiting for", the time reads "5 days" ("today"), never "Waiting ... · Waiting 5 days", with the wait's tone kept (`waitSaidOnce` in lib/home-model.ts, used by the list rows and Home's Needs you tags). A wait with no known start time (a bare "Waiting" tag) next to such a line shows no tag at all (`pillSaidOnce`). Keys name the sample repo and "draft", so `swapDemoDrafts` drops them when the visitor leaves. Every other write keeps the gate; its Start line says "Claude AI".

**D4, component header.** One Figma status (`FigmaStatus`, `figmaLineKind`): never "Not linked to Figma yet / Add your Figma file" beside "Figma is ahead"; the hint shows only once build requests are read and only to a lead (`teamLead` on the sample team: the cast lead only, not the developer it plays). body.title: Tab-like controls: one logic, one selected look each, focus ring keyboard only
body.body:
## What changed and why

The owner wants one logic for tab-like controls, written once and applied everywhere. Today the Settings tabs could show a heavy blue rounded box on the selected tab, the token type filter marked its selected segment with a Deep Harbor outline that reads as keyboard focus, and count tags changed look when selected. Agent-authored (Claude), session linked below.

### The rule (Tabs.docs.json, SegmentedControl.docs.json, docs/DESIGN-LANGUAGE.md section 7, AGENTS.md "UI quality bar")

- **Tabs (underline)** switch the SECTIONS or PANELS of one page or object: Settings (Team, Reviews, Tools, You), a component page (Usage, Tokens, Code, Changelog), the color families in the token editor.
- **SegmentedControl** switches a VIEW or a FILTER of the same content: List, Grid or Board; the token type filter; Light or Dark; compare Side by side or Overlay; the expression picker.
- Never a third look, never custom tab-like CSS.
- **Tabs selected** = ink text + the signal underline. Unselected = muted text. No box, no outline, no fill on the selection.
- **SegmentedControl selected** = raised plate on the subtle track (`surface.raised`, `border.emphasis` hairline, `elevation.raised`), ink text. Never a Deep Harbor or focus-colored outline.
- **Focus ring**: `:focus-visible` only (keyboard), inside the tab or segment a step off its edge (`focus-ring-width + focus-ring-offset`). A pointer focus draws nothing, the browser's ring included.
- **Counts** use the component's count slot and look the same selected or not.
- **Link mode** (segments with `href`) wears the same plate on the current page. `appearance="strong"` (the Deep Harbor fill) is explicit and used only by the global Library/Studio space switch.
- Tabs `variant="contained"` is deprecated (JSDoc + docs). It now wears the SegmentedControl plate, so there are still only two looks.

### Code

- `Tabs.module.css`: `.tab:focus:not(:focus-visible) { outline: none }`, an inset ring with offset, the selected count override removed, contained plate aligned with SegmentedControl.
- `SegmentedControl.module.css`: selected border `control-checked-bg` → `border-emphasis`. Link-mode `aria-current` no longer falls into the strong fill without `.strong`. Selected count overrides removed. Pointer-focus outline dropped. Inset ring with offset.
- Call sites: `SpaceSwitch.tsx` now passes `appearance="strong"`, so the space switch keeps its solid Deep Harbor current segment. `FaceSetting.tsx` face parts (Hair / Glasses / Beard / Expression panels) go from contained to underline Tabs, which also removes a contained-tabs-over-segmented stack. No site CSS restyled a selection (grep, and now a test enforces it).
- Not touched: `FamilyTabs.tsx` (token editor families still `variant="contained"`), which belongs to agent/token-explorer-fixes. By this rule it should drop `variant="contained"`.

### Tests

- New `apps/docs-site/src/lib/tab-like-controls.test.ts` checks CSS contracts on the DS sources. The react test project empties stylesheets and jsdom has no `:focus-visible`, so these run in the node docs project. Checks: the selected state uses the indicator or plate tokens and never focus-ring, outline or Deep Harbor (except under `.strong`); focus-ring tokens appear only under `:focus-visible`; no count rule is keyed by selection; no site stylesheet paints a selected segment or tab.
- React tests: link mode adds the strong class only with `appearance="strong"`; a clicked tab is selected, with axe.
- Ran: targeted vitest for Tabs, SegmentedControl, dom/segmented-control, FaceSetting, space-switch and the new contract test (all pass). Typecheck passes for react and docs-site. `npm run lint:css` passes. `npm run specs` regenerated. `npm run audit:docs` passes: 0 imitations, 100% adoption, no regression. No dev server, Storybook or browser run (CPU rule), so a reviewer needs to check the visuals.

## Risk tier

- [ ] Tier 1, low
- [x] Tier 2, medium: visual change to two DS components, a deprecated variant, AGENTS.md rule (owner-approved for this rule only)
- [ ] Tier 3, high

## Authored by

- [ ] Human
- [x] AI agent (Claude), reviewed by a human before merge

## Design review checklist

- [x] Uses tokens only (`npm run lint:css` passes)
- [x] Semantic tokens used in components
- [ ] Checked in Storybook in light and dark themes (reviewer: Settings tabs, token type filter, token editor segmented control, space switch, face parts in Settings > You)

body.title: Popup lists get an 8px inset; See it as matches Get started
body.body:
## What changed and why

Owner decision: the DS popup inset was too tight at 4px. Agent-authored (Claude Code).

- **DS (`@bridge-ds/react`, minor, visual change):** Menu, Select and Combobox popups pad with `var(--space-2)` (8px) instead of `var(--space-1)`. Item radius stays concentric: `calc(var(--popup-radius) - var(--space-2))`, which gives 20 - 8 = **12px on Bridge** (the existing `radius.control` / `radius.xl` step) and 16 - 8 = **8px on Ocean** (no primitive step at 8, but the calc keeps it exact, so no token is needed). Separators use `margin: var(--space-2) calc(var(--space-2) * -1)`: the inset's gap above and below, still running to the popup edge. No other DS component uses the popup item list inset (Popover is a content surface with `space-4`, SidebarNav is not a popup).
- **Combobox inline mode:** it has no popup surface, so no inset is added there: the always-open list keeps its edges aligned with the field above (the field-to-list gap is already `space-2`), and its items keep `radius-control`, which now equals the popup items' radius on Bridge. Note: Combobox's `.separator` class is not rendered by Combobox.tsx (only Select renders one); it was updated anyway for consistency.

body.body:
## What changed and why

Agent-authored (Claude Code). Two bugs the owner flagged on prod.

**Bug 1: Explorations Board paints one dataset, then another a second later.** Root cause found in the code: `reviews.ts loadList` painted every exploration's stage before its developers' task, its GitHub reviews and the team's library reviews were read (`readExplorationReviews` ran in the background). A handed-off copy exploration with a closed task read Ready to build first, then Shipped once the task landed (Review moderation drawer, out of the Board's 30-day Shipped column, so "8 explorations" became 7), and an exploration's reviews moved Contact page summary to Checking. Fixes:

- Explorations: the list reads where each exploration stands (tasks, reviews, team library reviews) and the closed list before its first paint (skeleton until then, at most 8 s so a hung read never holds it: `lib/settle-within.ts`).
- Home: leaves its skeleton only once the developers' tasks and the team's reviews are read.
- Kept browser copies are a failure fallback only: the kept team settings (#1105 `keptSite`) stand in only after this page's read failed (`noteTeamReadFailed`, set by `loadTeamModel` on a passing failure), never while the read is on its way. `loadTeamModel` already used the kept model only on failure; the failure path keeps its quiet line (`busy`).
- Versioned kept copies: `lib/kept-version.ts` tags every kept copy with a data shape (`KEPT_SHAPE`) and the app build (`__BRIDGE_BUILD__`, the deploy commit, defined in `astro.config.mjs`). Another build's copy is ignored and dropped: kept team settings, IndexedDB models (`repo-cache`), `ghGet`'s failure cache, the saved Explorations list, the Being built 5-minute lists. Every Studio page reading through `loadTeamData`/`loadTeamModel` (Home, Explorations, Being built, Library review, Products) gets this.
- Server SWR (`api/_lib/team-read.ts`): `SWR_MS` 10 min to 60 s. A visitor of the sample or public teams gets a kept answer at once only when it is younger than a minute; older, the read waits for GitHub and the kept answer stands in only on 429, 5xx or no answer (unchanged stand-in path).

**Bug 2: Dana's Home row for Sofia's "Order fulfilment timeline" named only the design review.** That exploration was asked before the two reviews (`leadAskedAt`, new pieces Card restyle and Timeline, no `library.askedAt`), so `libraryPendingOf` saw no library ask. `lib/team-reviews.ts legacyLibraryAsk`: while such a single ask waits (no design yes, not handed off), its new pieces wait for a library decision too. Dana's Home row now reads "Sofia's screen: your design review and a library decision" and the Explorations second line "Waiting for Dana's design review and library decision on Timeline".

- `repo-context.test.ts`: network answers, no cached first paint (kept settings and kept model never read when GitHub answers); network fails, kept copy plus the wait the page says; kept settings from an older build or shape ignored and dropped; a kept model of another build skipped by `getCachedModel` and the fallback.

- `review-lines.test.ts`: the legacy ask gives both hats on Dana's Home row and both reviews on the Explorations second line; none inferred once the design review answered.

body.title: Two reviews: the library decision and the design review
body.body:
## What changed and why

Builds the "two reviews" spec (draft PR #1124, docs/specs/two-reviews.md, now in this PR with the owner's answers). The one "In review" that waited on "the design lead" becomes two reviews with their own people: the **library decision** (design system owners decide what the library keeps, for every product, never off) and the **design review** (a product's reviewers check the screen before developers, a list per product, off per product). Agent-authored (Claude), owner approved the spec and its answers; normal PR, do not merge without review.

### Rules

- Done exploring asks the library owners only when the screen has something new for the library (a piece that is not the library as it is: core `asIsOption`, the rule of lib/library-as-is), and the product's design reviewers when its design review is on and someone other than the author can give it. Both start together and never wait on each other.
- Ready to build once the design review said Looks right (or there was none) **and** every new piece has a library answer (Add to the library, Keep in the screen only, Use an existing piece instead). Whichever answer comes last hands it off (`settleReviewsOnGitHub`). Neither review applies: straight to Ready to build, second line "No review needed: nothing new for the library, and Acme CRM has no design review".
- Design Needs changes: back to Exploring, library answers stay. Library Ask for changes on a piece: back to Exploring, the design yes stays and is not asked again; answering re-asks only what was asked.
- Nobody reviews their own exploration; the author as a product's only reviewer means no design review ("No design review: Dana is Acme Prints' only reviewer"); the only library owner decides on their own and it is recorded. An admin may answer either review, never asked.
- One status ladder, the reason as the second line (core `waitingFor`): "Waiting for Dana's design review", "Waiting for your design review and your library decision on Timeline", "Waiting for the library decision on Timeline".
- Library impact block: "Nothing new for the library" with no count; otherwise the count names new pieces only; pieces used as they are fold into "Everything else comes from the library".
- Home: one row per exploration naming the hat(s) ("Sofia's screen: your design review and a library decision"). Library review lists library decisions only ("12 library decisions wait for you, as design system owner", with the pointer to Explorations); the Explorations count counts design reviews.
- Sample team: Dana holds both hats; Acme CRM and Acme Prints design review = Dana; Leo's Deal pipeline cards reads "Waiting for Dana's design review" only.

### Data model and migration

- `bridge.config.json`: optional `products[].designReview` (`false` or `{ "reviewers": [...] }`, schema + core validation); absent reads as the design owners (Library off). `governance.owners.design` keeps its meaning, now worded "Decides what the library keeps".
- Exploration block: `lead*` fields become `design*` (`designAskedAt`, `designAskedTo`, `designTakenBy`, `designOkBy`, `askedPieces`); old names are read (core `withLegacyNames`, server copy in api/_lib/exploration-member held equal by a test) and written in the new names on the next write. New `designOkAt`, `library.askedAt/askedTo/askedBy`, `Decision.hat` (old decisions read as `design`).
- Server (email teams, api/_lib/review-settings.ts): `EmailMember.libraryOwner` (older `lead` reads as it); `bridge:design-review:<repo>` per product (`*` for every product not listed; reviewers = member refs, GitHub logins, or `any-designer`). Migration runs once on first read, idempotent: `one` -> design review on, the leads (no lead: the GitHub design owners); `shared` -> on, any designer, and every designer owns the library when nobody led; `shared-none` -> design review off without prompting, library decisions still asked; a team of one asks nobody (the author is never asked). Settings shows "Reviews now have two parts. Check who reviews each product's design." once. invites API: `set-library-owner` (`set-lead` kept) and `set-design-review`; `review-mode.ts` is only read by the migration.
- The proxy's lead gate is per exploration now (its product's design review, or new library pieces in its body).

### MCP and CLI

- `bridge_promote_exploration` returns `reviews: { design: { reviewers } | null, library: { owners, pieces } | null }`, `status` (`in-review` or `ready-to-build`) and `waitingFor`. For 2 releases it also returns `legacyStatus` (`waiting-for-lead`, `done-exploring`) and `leads` on `in-review`, documented as deprecated in docs/AI.md. No tool takes an exploration status as input. Because `status` values changed, `@bridge-ds/mcp` takes a **major** bump (the changeset says why); core, cli and docs-site stay minor.
- `bridge_continue_exploration`: `designReviewWords`, `libraryWords`, `libraryAnswers` per piece; `leadWords` stays as a deprecated alias for 2 releases (as do core `askLeadOnGitHub`, `leadApproveOnGitHub`, `isWaitingForLead`).
- `bridge_list_explorations`, `bridge_get_review`, `bridge_list_reviews`: `waitingFor`. `bridge_what_needs_me`: `hat` on every item and an `explorations` list with `hats`. `bridge_get_settings` / `bridge_get_config`: both roles. Server instructions say the two reviews in one sentence.
- CLI `bridge explore done` / `bridge explore list` print the same words.

### Bugs fixed

- Library review subtitle vs list count (11 vs 12): subtitle, list and sidebar now share one count (`lib/library-queue.ts`); the subtitle no longer depends on the page's filters.
- Timeline before/after preview: a new component shows only its after side, captioned "New in this screen", never the word "none" next to an empty tile.

### Not done / follow-ups

- The author's card keeps one current Stepper step (no new prop) and lists each waiting review inside it on its own line, naming who and the hat ("Dana reviews the design", "Dana decides on Timeline for the library").
- Settings > Reviews: editing stays admin-only; members read it with one quiet line, "Only admins change who reviews."
- Copy that assumed one person for both reviews ("your DS lead", "The design lead decided", "Dana decides what the library keeps" on screens with nothing new) now names the hat: the design reviewer or the library owners. Left as is on purpose: access requests, suggest-mode copy, marketing pages, build check role names.
- "Design review turned off while explorations wait" and "reviewer removed from the team": the pure rules exist (core `afterDesignReviewOff`, `withoutReviewer`, tested); the server does not yet sweep waiting explorations when the setting changes.
- The MCP reads reviews from bridge.config.json only, not the server settings of email teams.
- No screenshots: the owner asked for no dev server or browser on this machine. UI quality bar to be checked on the preview.

## Risk tier

- [ ] Tier 1, low
- [x] Tier 2, medium: new Studio section and behaviour, additive config field, MCP output values (owner approved, opened as a normal PR)
- [ ] Tier 3, high

## Authored by

- [ ] Human
- [x] AI agent (Claude), reviewed by a human before merge

## Design review checklist

- [x] Uses tokens only (`npm run lint:css` passes)
- [x] Semantic tokens used in components, not primitives
- [ ] Checked in Storybook in light and dark themes (not run locally: CPU constraint, CI and preview)
- [ ] Accessibility panel in Storybook (component tests run axe on Settings > Reviews, Library review and Library impact)
- [ ] Stories added or updated for every new state (no DS component changed)
- [x] Changeset added (mcp: major, core, cli, docs-site: minor)
- [x] No lint rule disabled, no test or story deleted
- [ ] Screens comment reviewed (pending preview)

## Checks run locally

Typecheck (core, docs-site, mcp, cli, figma-plugin): clean. `npm run audit:docs`: imitations 0 (0 since baseline). `npm run lint:css`: clean. Targeted vitest on every touched file (core two-reviews rules and GitHub flows, server settings and migration, team-reviews, Settings > Reviews keyboard + axe, Library review, Library impact, exploration page, Home, MCP explorations, CLI explore): all pass. Full suite and Storybook build left to CI.

body.title: Home tour takes no room: no blank space in the hero, the step floats beside what it points at
body.body:
## What changed and why

Owner-flagged prod bug on the Studio Home (`?as=sofia`, also dana and leo): since #1108 the tour popover ("Where to start", "Changes wait for the lead") reserved its own blank block under its anchor (`.dh-tour-room`, measured height set inline), so the Harbor hero turned into a tall empty blue block (~450px under the waves) with the popover floating in it.

The tour is now a transient overlay that takes no room:

- **Reserved space deleted**: the `room` state, the `.dh-tour-room` span and its CSS, and `TOUR_ROOM` are gone. The hero keeps its natural height whether the tour is open or not.
- **Zero-size anchors**: below a block (rows, cards), the anchor is `position: absolute` on the block's bottom edge (out of the flow, no grid gap; the old one used a negative margin that only matched one container's gap). Beside a control, it is a zero-width flex item next to the hero's primary button (`.sh-start` has no gap, so the row keeps its size).
- **Placement**: "Where to start" now floats beside "Start an exploration" (`side="inline-end"`, `align="start"`), over the harbor's sky and drawing, with the arrow on the button. It never covers the button or the headline. On a phone the DS Popover's collision handling (Base UI `fallbackAxisSide: 'end'`) flips it under the button and keeps it inside the viewport. The other steps still float under the rows or cards they talk about.
- **Phone inline-card mode removed** (`InlineStep`, `tourPlacement`): it pushed the hero and the sections down. On a phone the step now floats too and may overlap content below, inside the screen (`max-width: min(320px, 100vw - 16px)`). The scroll-into-view stays: it scrolls and never resizes anything.
- `StudioHome.tsx`: only the hero's `tour?.('start')` moved into `.sh-start` with `'beside'`, the `HomeTour` type takes the optional place, and two comments changed. Queue rows and review wording are untouched (agent/two-reviews owns them). `Needs`/`Explorations` still render the anchor in a narrow or wide spot, and both now end up in the same place. That cleanup can come later.

**Tests**: `HomeTour.test.ts` adds "takes no room in the hero". It renders the empty contributor Home with the tour open and with it done, and the hero markup is identical except for the zero-size anchor and Base UI's fixed, clipped helpers. Nothing in the hero gets an inline size, the step is portaled outside the hero, and the CSS contract holds (`.dh-tour-anchor-below` is absolute with `block-size: 0` and no margin, `.dh-tour-anchor-beside` has `inline-size: 0`, `.sh-start` has no gap, no `.dh-tour-room`). `tourSide` gives the right sides. The phone tests in `StudioHome.test.ts` now assert a floating step instead of an inline card.

Agent-authored (Claude Code). Per the owner's CPU constraint, no dev server, browser or Storybook build ran locally, so there are no screenshots here. CI and the Screens comment cover them.
