**Data (P0):**
- `POST /api/account { action: 'face', face }` keeps the face recipe on the account and writes it to `bridge:team:faces:<repo>` for each of the person's teams (`api/_lib/team-faces.ts`). The server refuses a hair style someone on one of their teams already saved: 409 `face_taken`, "Sofia already wears this hair style in Acme Design. Shuffle or pick another one." A hand-picked look-alike is allowed silently. Deleting the account frees the face; a rename moves it to the new seed.
- The team read (`GET /api/contribute?members=1`) returns `faces: { saved, order }`: the saved faces of people still on the team, plus who joined first.
- `lib/team-faces.ts teamDrawings` generalises `FACE_DRAWING_SEEDS`: saved faces claim first (first claim wins, a later one gets the nearest free style and a quiet nudge), the sample cast keeps its fixed drawings, everyone else gets their seed, else `seed#1`, `seed#2`... until the hair is neither taken nor a 20px look-alike (66 pairs measured at 20px plus variant02/variant37 by eye). One face for all teams, one Harbor surface for everyone, no new tokens.
- Every surface (`faces.tsx Who`, `scripts/people.ts`, `scripts/avatar.ts`, the account menu) now draws through `scripts/team-faces.ts faceUri`, so the saved and distinct faces show everywhere and repaint on save (`bridge:faces`).
- Sample team: Save keeps the played person's face in this browser only, said in one line; the cast stays as drawn for everyone.
- **DS RadioGroup `appearance="tile"`** (Tier 2, additive): the honest DS answer for picture options. The DS had no tile appearance (ChoiceCard keeps a radio circle, SegmentedControl is a bar of a few labelled segments and does not fit 64 pictures), so instead of hand-drawing tiles in Studio the RadioGroup gets a minimal tile appearance: wrapping rows of equal tiles (flex, so the Figma specs still read it; `npm run specs` regenerated), hidden but focusable radio, checked edge + selected surface, focus ring on the tile, disabled picture grey. With a `Tile` story, an `AllStates` specimen, docs (whenToUse, a don't, accessibility, anatomy) and a keyboard + axe test.
- `@bridge-ds/react/avatar-illustrated` gains `FaceRecipe`, `faceRecipe(seed)`, `illustratedFaceSvg`, `illustratedFaceUri`, `FACE_PART_VARIANTS` (additive, minor): the only way to draw a face from its parts.

Not in this PR (restrained on purpose): human words for all 64 hair styles (tiles are "Hair style 12", "Glasses 3"), a drawn face for photo users, the self-hosted Settings page, the nightly check, a phone layout.

body.title: TabsPanel outside its Tabs root: the last docs imitations go
body.body:
## What changed and why

The last 4 DS imitations on the docs site were the Team Settings group panels, hand-written `role="tabpanel"` divs under the DS Tabs island (SettingsTabs.tsx, #1110). The 4 Library component page panels (ComponentView.tsx) had the same shape and were hidden behind ignore comments (#1122). Both now use one documented DS way. Agent-authored (Claude Code).

**Why option (a), a linked panel, and not (b), panels inside the Tabs root.** Moving the panels inside the root means wrapping the groups in the Tabs island. The Settings groups hold `client:only` islands, so they would turn into Astro slot HTML inside a React island. Base UI would also render the panels hidden on the server, so the page could no longer be read without JavaScript, and an old anchor (#roles) would show the wrong group until hydration. The component page panels are server-rendered on purpose so the page reads without JavaScript. With (a), nothing moves: the island keeps the tabs and the page keeps its panels, which are now DS components.

**DS (Tier 2, additive, `@bridge-ds/react` minor):**
- `TabsPanel` outside a `Tabs` root (detected through the Tabs context; Base UI's panel throws there) renders a **linked panel**: the same `.panel` class plus `.linked`, `role="tabpanel"`, `tabIndex=0`, `aria-labelledby={tabId}`, `data-tabs-panel={value}`. It starts shown, so a page without JavaScript reads every panel. New prop `tabId`, which is ignored inside the root, where Base UI wires both ids. `.linked` keeps the page's text size (`font-size`/`line-height: inherit`), because a linked panel holds sections of the page itself. I measured this: without it, both pages would drop from 16/24 to 14/20.
- `showTabsPanel(scope, value)` in `@bridge-ds/react/dom` shows the picked linked panel and hides the others in that scope, so two tab sets on one page stay apart.
- Tabs.docs.json (when to use, accessibility, anatomy `linked`), a `LinkedPanels` story, and tests: ARIA wiring, axe, shown without script, keyboard picks a tab, then showTabsPanel shows its panel and Tab reaches it, and helper scoping.

**Docs site:**
- `pages/team-shell/settings`: the 4 groups are `<TabsPanel className="set-group" value id tabId data-set-group>`. They are static (no client directive), and Astro strips the static slot wrapper, so the islands inside are untouched. `scripts/settings-sections.ts` shows the groups with `showTabsPanel`.
- `ComponentView.tsx`: the 4 panels are `TabsPanel` with `componentTabPanelId` / `componentTabButtonId`. The 4 ignore comments are gone. `scripts/component-page.ts` uses `showTabsPanel`.
- The duplicated focus ring, radius and `[hidden]` rules in settings.css and library.css are removed, since the DS panel brings them.
- The SettingsTabs and ComponentTabs test fixtures now render the panels with the real `TabsPanel`.
- `apps/docs-site/src/data/audits/bridge-site-after.json` was regenerated by the audit itself (`bridge audit apps/docs-site/src --label "Bridge docs site, after" --json ...`), with no hand edits.

**Audit:** imitations **0** (-29 since the old baseline), 34 ignored on purpose (all by comment, none for tab panels any more). Token and component adoption are both 100%.

Verified on localhost (Playwright, 1280 wide):
- `#roles` opens Reviews and `#figma` opens Tools.
- Clicking Tools writes `#set-group-tools`.
- ArrowRight + Enter selects You, and Tab moves focus into its panel.
- `/components/button/#props` opens Code, and clicking Changelog / Usage writes `#changelog` / `#usage`.
- Computed text is 16px/24px, the same as the parent, with no page errors.

Checks: `npm run typecheck`, the react + docs vitest projects (447 files, 5105 tests), `npm run audit:docs`, `npm run lint:css` and `npm run specs` all pass. Tabs specs are unchanged. `npm run specs` also rewrites NumberField entries that have already drifted on main, so I left them out of this PR.

## Risk tier

- [ ] Tier 1, low: docs, stories, lint or a11y fixes, no visual or API change
- [x] Tier 2, medium: new component, variant or prop (additive). Opened as draft until design review
- [ ] Tier 3, high: token added/changed/removed, breaking API, or guardrail change. Design + tech owner approval required

## Authored by

- [x] AI agent (Claude), reviewed by a human before merge

## Design review checklist

- [x] Semantic tokens used in components, not primitives, for color and elevation

- [x] Accessibility panel in Storybook shows no violations; keyboard focus is visible (axe in unit tests)

body.body:
## What changed and why

Bridge sells design system mastery, and Studio Tokens built its controls by hand. `bridge audit` (#1117) listed 18 imitations in the token explorer and editor, plus 10 hand-drawn style sheet rules in `token-explorer.css`. They are now the design system's own components: small React islands the vanilla explorer mounts (the FamilyTabs pattern of #1118: one root per editor or page, its node moved into each redraw), or the `@bridge-ds/react/dom` renderers for rows built in strings. Behaviour, deep links (`?focus=`, `?component=`, `?t=`), keyboard paths and the draft flow are unchanged. Agent-authored (Claude), see the session link below.

### Counts (`node packages/cli/dist/index.js audit apps/docs-site/src --md`)

| | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Imitations in `components/explorer/**` and `scripts/explorer/**` | 18 | 0 |
| Imitations site-wide (after rebase on #1121 and #1122) | 121 on #1117 | 4 |
| Hand-drawn rules in `styles/token-explorer.css` (cssImitations) | 10 | 0 |
| `npm run audit:docs` | pass | pass |

### Conversion table

| Was | Now |
| --- | --- |
| `index.ts` type chips, `aria-pressed` buttons (`.xp-chip-btn`) | DS **SegmentedControl** with counts, `TypeFilter.tsx` |
| `index.ts` "Used by X" chip (`.xp-chip-filter`) | DS **Tag** with `onRemove` |
| `index.ts` row menu, `role="menuitem"` strings (`.xp-rowmenu-pop`) | DS **Menu** (`RowMenu.tsx`): the row's button is swapped for the DS trigger while open, then restored with focus; the action runs after the close |
| `index.ts` Library tree (`.xp-tree-btn`, twists) | DS **SidebarNav** / SidebarNavItem as buttons with counts (`CollectionTree.tsx`); subgroups show while their group is picked |
| `inline-edit.ts` ramp, `role="radio"` swatches + `role="radiogroup"` with a dynamic class (`.xe-sw`, `.xe-step`) | DS **SegmentedControl** of swatches (colors) / DS **RadioGroup** of steps (sizes, durations), `RampPicker.tsx` |
| `inline-edit.ts` `.xe-tip` hover tip | DS **Tooltip** (`data-tooltip`, `bindTooltips`) |
| `inline-edit.ts` More families (`.xe-tab-more`, `role="menu"`) | DS **Menu** with a ghost DS Button trigger, inside `FamilyTabs.tsx` |
| `inline-edit.ts` More options (`.xe-more-btn`) | DS **Button** ghost sm with `aria-expanded` (`MoreOptionsToggle.tsx`) |
| `inline-edit.ts` `class="xe-tabs"` wrapper | renamed `xe-families` (layout only) |
| `FamilyTabs.tsx` `data-xe-family-tab` on Tab (audit data-attr hit) | `data-xe-fam` |
| `TokenEditorKit.astro` review `aside role="dialog"` + scrim (`.xe-sheet`) | DS **Dialog** (ScriptDialog, `dialogHtml`, size lg): focus trap, Escape, scrim, stacked under the propose dialog |
| `TokenEditorKit.astro` `.xe-bar-count` + `.xe-bar-dot` | DS **Badge** with `dot` |
| `TokenExplorer.astro` `.xp-count` | DS **Badge** |
| `detail.ts` / `review.ts` contrast `.xp-badge`, `.xe-badge` | DS **Badge** via `badgeHtml` (new `icon` option) |
| `detail.ts` / `cells.ts` alias `.xp-chip`, `.xp-chip-flag` | DS **Tag** via new `tagHtml` in a plain button; the brand override flag a DS **Badge** |

`@bridge-ds/react/dom`: new `tagHtml()` (static Tag), an `icon` option on `badgeHtml()`, the `ellipsis` glyph and a `tabindex` override on `iconButtonHtml()`, all parity tested against the React components (minor bump).

Dead CSS removed: chips, chip buttons, badges, the swatch tip, ticks, steps, More families menu, row menu popup, the review sheet, scrim and head, the draft dot, the tree buttons and twists.

### After rebasing on #1122

`buttonHtml` / `iconButtonHtml` / `drawerHtml` from #1122 are used as they are (it converted the detail drawer, the editor's Cancel and Apply, the review's undo and the close buttons). This PR adds the grid's row-actions button: `.xp-rowmenu` is now `iconButtonHtml('ellipsis', ...)`; `iconButtonHtml` gains the `ellipsis` glyph and lets `attributes.tabindex` replace its default (the grid cell is roving, `-1`), both parity tested.

Not reported by the audit, follow-up: the cell editor popover itself (`.xe-pop`, role dialog set from script): a DS Popover has no anchor to a grid cell or bottom sheet mode.

### Tier 2 notes (no imitation, closest DS component used)

- **SegmentedControl swatch ramp**: a 12-step palette ramp needs a compact swatch-only segment (no gap or padding for a hidden label) or a ColorRamp component. With today's segments the editor widens (about 550 px) to show every step; on a phone the ramp scrolls with the DS fade. The tick row (0, 500, 950) is gone; each swatch has its name and hex as accessible name and DS tooltip. The "was" dot on the starting swatch is gone (the pick row still says "was neutral.0").
- **Menu anchor**: DS `MenuContent` has no `anchor` (Base UI Positioner has one), so a menu for one row of a large vanilla table swaps the row's button for the DS trigger while open.

One primary action per view (New token; Apply in the editor; the send button in the review). Light and dark checked, desktop 1389 and phone 390 (editor as a bottom sheet, review dialog full height).

body.title: Library and site: the real DS components, no more hand-made copies
body.body:
## What changed and why

Bridge sells design system mastery, and `bridge audit` (#1117) found our own Library, homepage and site drawing hand-made copies of DS components. This PR replaces them with the real components from `@bridge-ds/react`, keeps behaviour, anchors, a11y and tests, and deletes the hand-made CSS that became dead. Agent-authored (Claude Code), reviewed by a human before merge.

**Imitations (`node packages/cli/dist/index.js audit apps/docs-site/src`): 121 on main after #1118; 29 on this branch rebased on #1121 (all left are token explorer files and team-shell settings).** In the Library and site area: 41 before, **0 after**, 14 justified ignores (reasons below). The rest of the 55 removed are the site-wide `.btn` / `.icon-btn` sweep and the drawers, which reached Studio and explorer files.

To do it on pages built in plain scripts, `@bridge-ds/react/dom` gets two more renderers, each with parity tests against its React component:
- `buttonHtml()`, `buttonClassName()`, `iconButtonHtml()`: the exact markup of Button and IconButton (an `<a>` with `href`).
- `drawerHtml()`: the exact markup of Drawer. It opens and closes with the Dialog functions (`openDialog`, `closeDialog`), so focus trap, Escape, scrim click, scroll lock and focus return come from the DS.

Other agents: reuse `buttonHtml` / `iconButtonHtml` / `drawerHtml` (and `components/ds/StaticDrawer.astro` for an Astro drawer with slot content) rather than adding your own.

### Conversion table

| Where | Before (hand-made) | After (DS) |
|---|---|---|
| `styles/site.css` `.btn`, `.btn-primary/-accent/-secondary/-sm` | 24 string usages in scripts (requests, explorations, explorer detail and inline edit, history, visual impact, token editor) | `buttonHtml` (Button), CSS deleted |
| `styles/site.css` `.icon-btn` | 3 usages (explorer detail close x2, review undo) | `iconButtonHtml` (IconButton), CSS deleted |
| `styles/site.css` `.scope-chip` | brand colour dot in ScopeMenu | false positive: a swatch, renamed `.scope-brand-dot` |
| Visual impact Show diff (`aria-pressed`) | hand-made toggle | Button `pressed` |
| Foundations token rows: Copy as menu (`role="menu"`, `menuitemradio` x3 per row) | details popover per row | one DS SegmentedControl "Copy as" per page, in the page header |
| Foundations `.fd-chip` "Used by N" | details summary drawn as a chip | DS Button (secondary, sm) that opens its list (`aria-expanded`); "Unused" is a DS Badge |
| Foundations `.fd-toast` | hand-made toast | DS Toast (`PageToaster` island, `lib/page-toast.ts`) |
| Foundations `.fd-drawer`, LibraryShellKit and TokenDetailDrawer `role="dialog"` aside + scrim | hand-made drawer | DS Drawer (`drawerHtml`, `lib/token-drawer.ts`); its header names the token |
| Studio Components drawer `role="dialog"` aside + scrim | hand-made drawer | DS Drawer (`StaticDrawer.astro`), title = component, description = family |
| `.fd-pv-chip` | colour swatch named chip | false positive: renamed `.fd-pv-swatch` |
| Homepage step tabs (`role="tablist"`, `tabpanel`, `.hp-tab`) | hand-made vertical tabs | DS Tabs vertical (`HpSteps.tsx` island), autoplay, pause on hover and focus, reduced motion kept |
| Homepage drawn dialog `.hp-btn`, `-deep`, `-line` | spans drawn as buttons | DS Buttons inside the inert drawing |
| `/start/` `.gs-shape-button` | span drawn as a button | DS Button inside the inert, aria-hidden art |
| HpLead, Studio components drawer, LibraryEditMode typed " · " | separator spans | `SEP` / `joinSep` from `lib/sep.ts` |
| ComponentTabs `data-tab` | hook on the DS Tab | removed; LibraryEditMode finds the tab by its id |

### Justified ignores (Tier 2 notes)

- **Search palette** (`PaletteField` combobox, `Layout` listbox): the WAI-ARIA combobox with an always-open listbox inside the DS Dialog. The DS Combobox is a popup anchored to its input and has no inline-list mode. **Tier 2 request: a Command / inline-list Combobox.**
- **Component page panels** (ComponentView `tabpanel` x4): static panels of the DS Tabs island (#1118). A TabsPanel must render inside the Tabs root, and these stay server-rendered so the page reads without JavaScript. **Tier 2 request: a static TabsPanel for islands.**
- **Library and Studio switch** (`space-switch.css` x2): one navigation link that loads the other space. A Switch or SegmentedControl is a form control with a checked state, the wrong semantics. **Tier 2 request: a link mode for SegmentedControl.**
- **Token specimens** (`.sp-*` x5 in foundations.css): inert, aria-hidden miniatures drawn from the documented system's own tokens (a team's on its Library), so they cannot be Bridge's components.
- **Lead board drawing** (`.hp-ldec-chip`): chips inside the aria-hidden picture, scaled with the drawing unit; a Tag has fixed control sizes.

body.title: Library review counts: Badge appearance count, ink on a neutral fill
body.body:
## What changed and why

The owner flagged the count tag as washed out: muted text on the neutral status fill with a hairline border, 5.08:1, which read as disabled. **Owner decision:** keep the current count style in the sidebar and in Tabs and SegmentedControl, and apply the new style **only in Library review** (the group and chapter counts such as Foundations 5 and Colors 4, plus every other count rendered by Library review's `Count`).

- **Badge `appearance="count"`** is a new value of an existing prop (additive, Tier 2). The number uses `--color-text-default` in medium weight with tabular figures and no letter spacing, centred, at the caption size (12/16, from the new type scale #1100 and the sweep #1119). It sits on `--color-border-emphasis` as the fill, with no border. Inside a current or selected item (`aria-current`, `aria-selected="true"`, `aria-checked="true"`, `data-active` on an ancestor) it takes the stronger tone, `--color-surface-inverse` with `--color-text-inverse`. `tone` is ignored.
- **Library review**: `Count` (LibraryReview.tsx) renders `appearance="count"`, and its local tabular-nums rule is gone.
- **Unchanged on purpose**: Tabs, SegmentedControl and SidebarNav keep their count slot, and the Studio side nav, CountTag, component families, list filters and selects keep their current rendering.
- Docs: the Badge docs JSON scopes the count to group headings in review lists and points navigation and tab counts to their component's `count` prop. It also gets a do example, an accessibility line and the `count` anatomy key. The Badge story gains `Count` and count specimens in AllStates. `component-specs.json` is regenerated.
- Tests: the new `Badge.test.tsx` checks the classes, that the tag has no role, that `tone` is ignored and that the accessible name holds inside a current item, and runs axe on both cases.

Agent-authored (Claude Code), session https://claude.ai/code/session_01DyWiXiGdydo1jH3rNhdj6N.

### Why the emphasis neutral as fill, and no border

- Library review groups sit on tinted cards (#edeff2 in light), the same value as `feedback.neutral.bg`, so the old fill vanished there (1.00:1) and only the hairline remained. `bg.muted` is only 1.07:1 on that ground, and in dark it is 1.00:1 on `surface.raised`. `border.emphasis` (neutral.300 / neutral.700) is the one existing neutral step that stays visible on every ground while keeping the ink at 7:1 or more in all four brand and theme pairs.
- **Non-text 3:1:** no existing fill can reach 3:1 against white and still carry ink at 7:1 (a fill at 3:1 caps dark text near 5.5:1). Meeting both would take a `border.strong` border, which is heavier than the problem. The tag is not interactive and the figure carries the information, so WCAG 1.4.11 does not ask for a boundary. I kept no border.
- **Token note (Tier 3, not done here):** `border.emphasis` is described as a hairline. If the owners want the role to be explicit, the follow-up is a component token `badge.count.bg` aliasing `{color.border.emphasis}`, plus a `contrast.checks.json` pair for `text.default` on it at 7:1 or more. I did not add it.
- **Type scale:** rebased on #1100 and #1119. The count follows caption 12/16, the sweep's rule for counts, through the existing caption tokens, and no type token changed.

### Measured before / after (Library review counts)

Before = prod with computed styles. After = the same pages with this PR's count rule applied. 12px / 16px line height, weight 500, tabular-nums, 20px tall, 8px side padding, before and after.

| Context | Before (text on fill, border, ratio) | After (text on fill, border, ratio) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Group card (Foundations 5, Colors 4), light | #5b6672 on #edeff2, 1px #e3e8ee, **5.08:1**, fill 1.00:1 vs card | #15202b on #c6cfd9, none, **10.47:1**, fill 1.37:1 vs card |
| Group card, dark | #a0aab5 on #323e4c, **4.62:1** | #f5f7f9 on #495562, **7.09:1**, fill 2.17:1 vs card |
| Ocean light | #5e6e7d on #ecf0f3, **4.58:1** | #162839 on #c3cfdb, **9.50:1** |
| Ocean dark | #9eabb8 on #2d3f50, **4.63:1** | #f4f7fb on #455666, **7.04:1** |
| Inside a current item | same as rest | #ffffff on #15202b, **16.49:1** light; #0b1825 on #edeff2, **15.56:1** dark |
| Compact density | 20px, 8px padding | same: the count uses fixed size tokens |

body.title: Studio: the DS components instead of hand-made copies (45 imitations to 9)
body.body:
## What changed and why

Studio had hand-made copies of design system components that `bridge audit` now reports as imitations (#1117). This PR swaps them for the real `@bridge-ds/react` components, deletes the CSS that became dead, and marks the true exceptions with the audit's ignore comment and a reason. Agent-authored (Claude), session linked below. Part of the imitations sweep: the Library agent owns the `.btn` HTML strings, another owner the Studio components index page.

**Imitations in the Studio area (components/ds/studio, Studio CSS, scripts/reviews, scripts/history, requests, explorations, github-session, StudioHeader): 45 before, 9 after.** Whole site: 125 on #1117, 85 now with this branch on today's main.

The 9 left are handed off, not exceptions:

- 8 `.btn` class strings in `scripts/explorations.ts` (2), `scripts/requests.ts` (3), `scripts/history/page.ts` (1), `scripts/reviews/visual-impact.ts` (1 link and the "Show diff" toggle): the Library agent swaps them with its `buttonHtml` renderer (agent/imitations-library), as agreed. I left those lines alone to avoid conflicts. The "Show diff" toggle should become `buttonHtml` with `pressed`, a single toggle, not a SegmentedControl.
- `styles/components-studio.css` `.cm-drawer`: its markup lives in `pages/studio/components/index.astro`, which another agent owns; it needs the `drawerHtml` renderer from the same Library PR.

### Conversions

| Where | Was | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| LibraryReview: designer's "who decides" note | `.lr-banner` (tinted box) | `Banner appearance="neutral"`, lead's face on the title line, link in `actions` |
| LibraryReview: decided, with Undo | `.lr-toast` fixed stack | DS `Toast` (`ToastProvider` + `useToast`): Undo action while it waits, the send's answer after |
| LibraryReview: One by one on a phone | IconButtons around "3 of 12" (`.lr-compact-count`) | `Pagination variant="compact"` |
| LibraryReview: eyebrow dot | typed `·` span | shared `Sep` (lib/sep) |
| LibraryMap: "5 of 12" | `.lr-map-focus-count` span | `Badge tone="neutral" size="sm"` |
| ExplorationParts ShotLink | `.xp-shotlink-pill`, `.xp-shotlink-chip` | `Button variant="secondary"` rendered on a span (inert: the whole capture is the link), `Tag size="sm"` on touch |
| AdoptionReport values and token names | `<code class="ar-tag">` | `TokenValue size="sm"` (swatch off where the row already shows one) |
| reviews.ts token table: added, removed | `.rv-kind-tag` | `badgeHtml` success, danger, neutral |
| visual-impact filters | `.rv-seg` with `aria-pressed` buttons | `segmentedControlHtml` (new), arrow keys via `bindSegmentedControls` |
| visual-impact Before, After labels | `.vi-tag` pills | `badgeHtml` solid |
| history token panel: demo switch | `.hs-switch` button | `switchHtml` (new) |
| history token panel: demo note | `.hs-banner` | `badgeHtml` warning + `t-meta` line (dev builds only) |
| ChangelogView announcement | `.announce-avatar` box with an icon | `Avatar kind="agent"` decorative |
| BranchReview, ChangesMode, github-session `prLinksHtml` | typed " · " | `SEP` from lib/sep |
| ProductPage library-ask cards | DS Link with a `.sh-choice-btn` class | same Link, `.sh-choice-link` (it is the card's primary link, never a button) |
| LibraryImpact summary tail | `.li-count-tail` | `.li-summary-tail`: the tail is "1 waits for you", not a count |
| NewBrandFlow hex field prefix | `.nb-chip` | `.nb-hex-swatch`: a square of the typed color, not a Tag |
| StudioHeader | `countId` slot `.st-count` | removed: no page ever passed it |
| Dead CSS deleted | `.rv-count`, `.rv-avatar`, `.rule-count`, `.deck-chip(s)`, `.ed-banner`, `.gh-dialog` box, head and foot, `.hs-switch*`, `.hs-banner`, `.lr-banner*`, `.lr-toast(s)`, `.ar-tag` | |

### Exceptions (ignore comment with the reason)

- `adoption-report.css .ar-pv-drawer`: a drawing of a Drawer on a thumbnail plate; the DS Drawer is a modal portal.
- `motion-changes.css .mc-pill`, `studio-home.css .sc-mockup-pill`: wireframe blocks inside drawings (no label, aria-hidden).
- `build-review.css .brv-stepper`: the bar of BuildReview's interactive stepper, already an accepted exception in BuildReview.tsx.
- `a11y.css .a11y-chip-key`: an 8px verdict dot, the legend key of the contrast table.
- `team-access.css .rail-chip`: the side nav slot of the TeamChip menu (a DS Button and Menu), with its rule.

### Separators

Typed " · " now go through `lib/sep` (`SEP`, the `Sep` part). The audit does not flag `{SEP}` or `${SEP}`, so no change to the audit was needed. A vertical `Divider` would draw a hairline, not the dot of a status line, so `SEP` stays the sanctioned separator.

### Tier 2 notes (DS gaps, not imitated)

- `Pagination` compact says "Page 3 of 12" and "Previous page": it has no item noun ("piece"). Wanted: a `noun` or labels prop.
- `Banner` has no Harbor-tinted appearance. The designer note was a light Harbor box and is now the neutral ground.
- `Avatar kind="agent"` needs a `brand` (only `claude`). The changelog announcement uses it decorative; a generic Bridge agent preset would be more exact.
- `@bridge-ds/react/dom` gains `switchHtml`, `bindSwitches`, `setSwitchChecked`, `segmentedControlHtml`, `bindSegmentedControls`, `selectSegment` (additive API, minor bump), with parity tests against the React components (same classes, state attributes, ARIA). The switch renders a native `<button role="switch">` where Base UI renders a span plus a hidden input, so Space, Enter and label clicks work with no script.

### Measured

- The Library review banner is about 64px tall instead of 78 (DS Banner padding, ui text instead of body), same width and left edge, the link on the same line on desktop and under the text on a phone.
- One by one on a phone: the pager's chevrons are the DS ghost IconButtons at size md, not secondary (bordered).

body.title: Type sweep: secondary lines in meta, 12px only for labels, role line heights everywhere
body.body:
Agent-authored (Claude Code). Risk tier 1 (CSS only: no token, prop or component added). Follows #1100, which the owner approved; this is the global pass on font sizes he asked for.

## Summary

Every rendered text in Studio and the Library now sits on a role of the new scale. Secondary lines (who and when, ages, descriptions under titles, card meta, column labels, setting help) read in `meta` 13/18 instead of 12px or 14px. 12px is left only for labels: section labels, table heads, badges, tags, counts, keys, code values. List row titles are UI 14 medium over their meta line, one step apart.

## How it was measured

Playwright crawl of 13 Studio pages for each of the five personas (`?as=dana|sofia|leo|malik|ann`) and 11 Library pages, at desktop 1389x868 and phone 390x844: every visible text node with its size, weight, line height and color, mapped to a role (`off-scale` when it matches none). Before: prod (with #1100). After: prod with this branch's CSS injected (same data on both sides). Specimen pages (Typography, Color, Spacing, Tokens) are left out of the counts: they show the scale on purpose.

## Roles per page (text nodes, all personas, desktop + phone)

Reading it: `meta` goes from 4 to 1,168 texts; 12px texts from 960 to 797 nodes, and from 92 to 57 distinct texts, all labels (below). `h3` drops where list row titles moved from a 16 semibold card title to a 14 medium row name. Off-scale drops from 2,170 to 1,239; what is left is mostly button and field labels (16.8 line inside a fixed-height control, harmless), the Tag component's 12/14.4 inside its pill, and quality numbers (16/32).

## The 12px texts left, each justified

| Kind | Examples | Why 12 |

| Table heads | Component, Person, Access, Examples, Tokens, In Figma, Used in | Column labels of a DS Table |

No sentence, name, date or description is at 12px any more.

## What changed

- **`brand.css`**: new `t-meta` utility; `t-ui t-muted` (muted UI text, a secondary line by definition) reads in meta. The home tour's explaining paragraph is exempt (stays UI).
- **73 rules moved to meta** in the Studio and Library styles. Among them:

  - Home and lists: row bylines, card who-and-when, mockup meta.
  - Settings, invites, account: setting help, people's role lines, intros.
  - Library impact, build review, suggestion review, review queue.
- **Row titles**: Home queue, Explorations and Being built rows (`.sh-row-title`), Library review side list and List view: UI 14 medium instead of 16, so a name sits one step over its 13 meta line.
- **Line heights**: 353 rules that set a role size without a line height now set the role's (14/20, 12/16, 13/18) instead of inheriting 1.5 of the size from the root (14/21, 12/18).
- **`packages/react`, size only**: Stepper step meta ("now, for 3 days") and Textarea counter read in meta. Count tags untouched (agent/count-tag-style owns their look).
- Library review, phone: the chapter names no longer drop to Fraunces 16 (the 21px floor of the display face).

body.title: Being built: every item shows where it comes from (lead-sent exploration or lead-approved library change)
body.body:
## What changed and why

Owner's rule (2026-11-12): build work only comes from (a) an exploration the design lead sent to developers, or (b) a library change the lead approved in Library review. Designers, developers and PMs never file build requests directly, so "Asked by Leo / Malik / Ann" on Being built was wrong. On the sample team, Explorations showed 0 Ready to build while Being built showed 3: those 3 (and most of the rest) were leftovers of the early demo, tied to no exploration.

- `apps/docs-site/src/lib/build-origin.ts` (new, tested): `buildOriginOf` / `withBuildOrigins` / `buildOriginLine`. Every Being built row must carry its origin:
  - an exploration handed to developers is its own origin ("Exploration Dana sent", from the lead's recorded Looks right), so Being built and Explorations list the same explorations;
  - a request or library branch states it: an `origin` in a Bridge block (core RequestOrigin exploration or adoption report, or `{"kind":"lead","approvedBy":"Dana"}`), a `bridge-origin` block, or the "Needed by" block of the branch opened for an exploration; the issue body first, then the body of the pull request doing the work ("From Contact page summary", "Library change Dana approved");
  - a push from Figma and Claude's fix from Figma: approved in Figma ("Library change approved in Figma");
  - anything else is not listed.
- `scripts/building-data.ts`: applies `withBuildOrigins` once where the rows are read, so the page, the Studio home line, a developer's "N build requests wait" and "Figma is ahead" on Bridge's own Library all read the same rows. No new GitHub read.
- `lib/building-page.ts` `personLine` takes an `origin` that replaces "Asked by X"; `lib/building-view.ts` `rowLine` passes it, exploration rows carry `sentBy` (`sentByOf`), and `slimBody` keeps origin blocks of long pull request bodies.
- `BeingBuilt.tsx`: small edits only (the card's `cardLine` and the detail's "Sent by" line say the origin; the unused requester helper goes).
- `scripts/build-origins-cleanup.mjs` (+ test): the sample team cleanup below, dry run by default, `--apply` to write. **Not run.**

**Coordination:** rebased on #1114 (agent/building-groups, merged). Its card line `cardLine` now falls back to the origin (`buildOriginLine(originOfRow(v))`) instead of the requester: "Malik · yesterday" once someone builds it, "Library change Dana approved · 2 days ago" before. An adoption report's origin stays its card note (with the link) so it is not said twice. `personLine` (list rows) takes the same origin.

**Product consequence to know:** on every team, a component change request filed directly (MCP `bridge_create_request`, CLI) without an origin no longer shows on Being built. It still exists on GitHub. The team Library page's "Figma is ahead" (`buildViewsFor`, no bodies read) is unchanged.

## Inventory: Being built on the sample team today (acme-design-demo/bridge-demo-ds)

Read once from GitHub (issues + pull requests of the DS repo, pull requests of acme-crm-design and acme-prints-design). Seeds: the 2026-11-08 "refile" (`apps/docs-site/api/_lib/demo-refile.ts` `DEMO_REQUESTERS`, `scripts/refile-demo-items.mjs`) filed #52 to #61 again for Leo, Sofia and Ann from the maintainer's #19, #37 to #43; Malik's #62 to #65 were opened the same day; the product explorations were seeded by `scripts/seed-demo-explorations.mjs`. No fixture in apps/docs-site feeds this page.

| Card (status) | Source | "Asked by" | Origin found | After this PR (no data change) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Toast: an undo action (Ready to build) | issue #58, labels component-change, product: account | Leo | none | hidden |
| Table: keep the header visible (Ready to build) | issue #59, component-change | Malik | none | hidden |
| Select: a search field (Ready to build) | issue #60, component-change | Sofia | none | hidden |
| Card: a subtle tone (Being built) | issue #56 + Malik's draft PR #64 | Leo | none | hidden |
| ProfileHeader (Checking) | issue #52 (product: account) + Malik's PR #62 | Ann | PR #62 "Needed by" Contact page summary (acme-crm-design#2) | From Contact page summary |
| Button: label while loading (Checking) | issue #55 + Malik's PR #63 | Ann | none | hidden |
| Avatar: xl size (Checking) | issue #57 (product: account) + Malik's PR #65 | Sofia | PR #65 "Needed by" Contact page summary | From Contact page summary |
| Contact page summary (Checking) | exploration acme-crm-design#2, task acme-crm#3 open | Sofia (done exploring) | itself; Looks right recorded by **Ann** (PM, never decides) | Exploration Ann sent (fixed by cleanup) |
| Review moderation drawer (Shipped) | exploration acme-prints-design#3, task acme-prints#2 closed done | Ann | itself; Looks right by Dana | Exploration Dana sent |
| Plan comparison (Shipped) | PR #48, explore/plan-comparison, merged 2026-10-25, product: account (removed) | Ann | itself, no lead decision recorded (old format) | Exploration sent to developers (archived by cleanup) |
| Spinner spins at full speed (Shipped) | issue #10 closed done + PR #11 | Leo | none | hidden |

## Cleanup plan for the sample team (awaiting owner approval, not executed)

`node scripts/build-origins-cleanup.mjs` (dry run) then `--apply`. 13 reads, 18 writes, idempotent, nothing deleted.

1. Lead-approved library changes (one per status), each gets `<!-- bridge-origin {"kind":"lead","approvedBy":"Dana",...} -->`, "Requested by Dana through Bridge." and a summary saying Dana approved it:
   - #59 Table sticky header: Ready to build
   - #56 Card subtle tone: Being built (Malik's draft #64)
   - #55 Button loading label: Checking (Malik's #63)
2. Library pieces of the Contact page summary exploration: #52 ProfileHeader and #57 Avatar xl get an exploration `bridge-origin` block (acme-crm-design#2), lose "**Product:** Account app" and the `product: account` label, summaries reworded to Acme CRM.
3. Close as not planned, with a comment: #58 Toast undo, #60 Select search.
4. Malik's PRs #62, #63, #64, #65: "Requested by Ann/Malik/Sofia." becomes "Approved by Dana." (words only).

7. Left as is: #10 Spinner (closed history, hidden by the rule), Order fulfilment timeline (acme-prints-design#1, waiting for Dana's decision: once she approves its Card and Timeline pieces in Library review they become build items "From Order fulfilment timeline"), suggestions #53, #54, #61.

After it: Ready to build 1 (Table), Being built 1 (Card), Checking 4 (ProfileHeader, Avatar xl from Contact page summary; Button; Contact page summary), Shipped 1 (Review moderation drawer). Every card says where it comes from; Explorations' Ready to build (0) matches the explorations on Being built, the one Ready to build card is a library change Dana approved.

Also suggested (not in the script): stop re-running `scripts/refile-demo-items.mjs` for requests; its `DEMO_REQUESTERS` table encodes designers asking for build work.

body.title: Spec: two reviews, the library decision and the design review
body.body:
Phase 1 of splitting "In review" in two: the **library decision** (design system owners keep or not a new piece) and the **design review** (a product's design lead checks the screen before developers, optional per product). Spec only, no code: `docs/specs/two-reviews.md`.

## What it settles

- Settings > Reviews gets two roles: "Decides what the library keeps" (team wide) and "Reviews the design before developers" (per product, can be off).
- Done exploring asks the library decision only when something is new, the design review only when the product has one, both in parallel; with neither it goes straight to Ready to build.
- Same status ladder; "In review" always carries who and why on its second line ("Waiting for Dana's design review").
- Library impact: "Nothing new for the library", no count, when nothing is new.
- Data model (`products[].designReview`, `libraryOwner` on members, design review asks in the exploration block), MCP impacts (`bridge_promote_exploration`, `bridge_continue_exploration`, `bridge_what_needs_me`), edge cases, and a migration where every team that had leads keeps a design review ON.

## Mocks

Made on the prod sample team with the real Studio CSS and DS components (text changed in the page), 1389 by 868 at 2x. Shared separately (not committed): Settings > Reviews, an exploration in each case (library + design review, design review only, nothing to review), Dana's Home rows, Library review with library decisions only.

## Open questions

Listed at the end of the spec (wait for both before Ready to build?, one reviewer or a list per product, aliases for old MCP names, where "Shared, no review" teams land, one Home row or two when one person holds both hats).

Risk tier: Tier 1 (docs only). Agent-authored.

body.title: Spec: Your face, optional drawn-avatar customizer with team-unique Shuffle
body.body:
Draft, docs only (`docs/specs/`). Agent-authored. Risk tier: none (no code); the spec itself flags one Tier 2 (Avatar `xl`) and one optional Tier 3 (tints).

## What this proposes

An optional **Your face** band in Settings > You: one quiet row (your face at 40px + **Change**), opening in place to an 80px preview, **Next to your team** (you and every teammate at 24px), **Shuffle**, and on demand **Pick the parts yourself** (Hair, Glasses, Beard, Expression). Shortcut: "Change your face" in the account menu.

**Uniqueness rule (measured).** At 20px, identity is the hair: hair changes the drawing 0.064, beard and glasses 0.007, eyes/brows/nose/lips 0.001 to 0.002. So within a team a hair style is worn by one person (hard rule, server 409 `face_taken`), and Shuffle also avoids 20px look-alikes (45 measured pairs of 2,016). Whole-face pixel distance alone fails: Dana vs the old Malik drawing measures farther apart than Dana vs Ann. New members get an automatic distinct drawing (`seed#n`), which generalises tonight's `FACE_DRAWING_SEEDS` so nobody writes an exception again. First claim wins across teams; Shuffle avoids taken styles of every team you are in.

**Storage.** A small recipe (part names) on the Bridge account (`POST /api/account { action: 'face' }`, like `aiTools`), plus a per-team face map (`bridge:team:faces:<repo>`) returned by the team read, so `drawFace(seed)` resolves it on every surface. Photo wins over drawing; sample team and no-account sessions keep it in the browser.

**Phases.** P0 no UI (recipe, team map, automatic distinct faces, nightly zero-identical check) fixes the collision alone; P1 row + Shuffle; P2 part pickers + taken states + menu shortcut; P3 photo/drawing choice, tints, phone.

Eight open questions for the founder are in section 14.

## Screens (desktop, 1389x868 @2x, real Bridge Library 1.8.6 + real face drawer)

1. Collapsed row
![collapsed](https://github.com/the-bridge-company/ai-design-system-demo/blob/agent/avatar-customizer-prd/docs/specs/avatar-customizer/1-collapsed.png?raw=true)

2. Open, Save disabled until a change
![open](https://github.com/the-bridge-company/ai-design-system-demo/blob/agent/avatar-customizer-prd/docs/specs/avatar-customizer/2-open.png?raw=true)

3. After Shuffle
![shuffled](https://github.com/the-bridge-company/ai-design-system-demo/blob/agent/avatar-customizer-prd/docs/specs/avatar-customizer/3-shuffled.png?raw=true)

4. Pick the parts: taken styles, "Taken by Sofia"
![parts](https://github.com/the-bridge-company/ai-design-system-demo/blob/agent/avatar-customizer-prd/docs/specs/avatar-customizer/4-parts-taken.png?raw=true)

5. Saved
![saved](https://github.com/the-bridge-company/ai-design-system-demo/blob/agent/avatar-customizer-prd/docs/specs/avatar-customizer/5-saved.png?raw=true)

6. Account menu shortcut
![menu](https://github.com/the-bridge-company/ai-design-system-demo/blob/agent/avatar-customizer-prd/docs/specs/avatar-customizer/6-account-menu.png?raw=true)

## UI quality bar, measured

- Alignment: preview, Shuffle, tabs, first tile and Save all start at x=616 (the Settings value column); collapsed label, face and Change share one centre line.
- 4 font sizes (30, 21, 14, 12), nothing under 12px; one primary action; controls at DS heights.
- Say it once: the uniqueness rule is one sentence in the row help and one in the Hair panel; taken tiles show only the name.
- Progressive disclosure: 7 interactive elements at level 0; the 31 of the parts level appear only on demand.
